statement: The starting relative category is (Cat,W), where W is a specified class of functors; the intended ordinary case is W∞, the functors whose nerves are weak homotopy equivalences.
repair: Read “catégorie de modèles” here as a category with weak equivalences, not as the assertion of a Quillen model structure. Work in fixed sufficiently large universes.
notes: Opening paragraph; recovered commentary p1. The example W_D is the class detected by an already given derivator D defined on all small categories; no construction of W_D is supplied here.

statement: A category A is W-aspherical when A→1 belongs to W; it is universally W-aspherical when every projection A×B→B belongs to W.
notes: Definitions used in L2, L2 bis, L3 bis and L3 ter.

statement: L1(a): every identity functor belongs to W.
notes: L1 is among the standing assumptions explicitly adopted on ms2.

statement: L1(b): for composable functors f and g, if two of f, g and gf belong to W, then the third belongs to W.
notes: Two-out-of-three; L1 is adopted on ms2.

statement: L1(c): for f:A→B and g:B→A, if gf and fg belong to W, then f and g belong to W.
notes: The third clause of the source’s “Saturation”; do not silently substitute a different list of saturation axioms.

statement: L2: the projection [1]×A→A belongs to W for every category A.
notes: Interval invariance. Listed as an axiom and subsequently claimed to follow from the standing package.

statement: L2 bis: the unique functor [1]→1 belongs to W.
notes: Source identifies this with L3′ of Pursuing Stacks; its numbering is distinct from the dual L3′ in the present manuscript.

statement: L3: every category having a terminal object is W-aspherical.
notes: One of the standing assumptions on ms2.

statement: Dual L3′: every category having an initial object is W-aspherical.
notes: Footnote 1; later claimed to follow from opposite invariance on ms2.

statement: L3 bis: every weakly contractible category, i.e. every category with weakly contractible nerve, is W-aspherical.
notes: Here Hot-aspherical means W∞-aspherical, not merely categorically contractible.

statement: L3 ter: if A has weakly contractible nerve, then A×B→B belongs to W for every category B.
notes: The universally W-aspherical strengthening of L3 bis; footnote 2 records that it implies L2 and L3.

statement: L3 quater: W∞⊆W; every weak homotopy equivalence of nerves is a W-equivalence.
repair: Cisinski proves W∞⊆W for a modern fundamental localizer defined using relative Theorem A (2004, Theorem 2.2.11). In this manuscript the inclusion is separately adopted at ms7 and must not be inferred from an unexamined replacement of absolute L4 by relative L4 bis.
notes: L3 quater is printed before the ms2 marker; footnote 5 at ms7 says it will be assumed throughout the sequel. Commentary p1.

statement: The displayed implication chain is L3 quater⇒L3 ter⇒L3 bis⇒L3, and L3 ter⇒L2⇒L2 bis.
repair: The implications use preservation of weak contractibility under product with an arbitrary category and contractibility of categories with terminal objects; the last implication is specialization to B=1.
notes: Two displayed implication chains before the ms2 marker; footnote 2 repeats part of the chain.

statement: A functor f:X→Y is W-aspherical when X/y→Y/y lies in W for every object y of Y. Under L1 and L3 this is equivalent to X/y being W-aspherical for every y.
notes: Parenthetical definition in L4; Y/y has terminal object id_y.

statement: Original L4 (absolute Theorem A): if f:X→Y is W-aspherical, then f belongs to W.
gap_or_error: This formulation tests comma categories over the target Y. It is not literally the later assertion about an arbitrary map X→Y over a third category S.
repair: Keep the original axiom distinct from relative L4 bis on ms44. The recovered commentary p2 derives the latter under the stronger package L1, L2 bis and original L5.
notes: “Axiome de localisation”; modern relative formulation: Cisinski (2004), Definition 1.1.3 and Remark 1.1.4.

statement: Dual L4′: if y\X→y\Y belongs to W for every y in Y, for f:X→Y, then f belongs to W; under dual L3′ this is equivalently W-asphericity of all y\X.
notes: Footnote 3; source later appeals to opposite invariance. The comma object y\X consists of arrows y→f(x).

statement: Original L5 (fibration descent): let X→S and Y→S be Grothendieck fibrations and f:X→Y a Cartesian functor over S. If every strict fibre map f_s:X_s→Y_s belongs to W, then the total functor f belongs to W.
gap_or_error: This is the fibrewise-to-total implication, not the total-to-fibrewise detection axiom renamed L5 on ms43.
repair: The first implication is available under the appropriate relative descent axioms; retain its Cartesian-functor and fibration hypotheses when using this original formulation.
notes: Commentary p1–p2; the two axioms called L5 must be distinguished in every cross-reference.

statement: The initial meaning of a fundamental localizer is a class W satisfying L1, L3 and original absolute L4; this package is assumed for the subsequent discussion.
gap_or_error: Its literal axiom list differs from the modern definition using relative Theorem A.
repair: State explicitly whenever relative L4 bis, original L5, or W∞⊆W is additionally used. The recovered commentary does not claim an independence theorem for the weaker list.
notes: “On va supposer ici aussi qu’on ait au moins L1, L3, L4”.

statement: The source asserts that L1, L3 and original L4 imply interval invariance L2.
gap_or_error: No derivation is supplied in this excerpt; the source refers back to the earlier localizer formalism.
repair: Direct elementary proof from the printed axioms: for π:A×[1]→A and a∈A, the comma category (A×[1])/a is canonically (A/a)×[1], with terminal object (id_a,1). Both this comma category and A/a therefore map to 1 by W-equivalences, by L3. Since π/a:(A/a)×[1]→A/a commutes with those maps, L1(b) gives π/a∈W. Original absolute L4 now gives π∈W, proving L2. Neither relative L4 bis nor original L5 is required; the excerpt merely omits this derivation.
notes: Parenthetical “impliquant L2”; commentary p1–p2.

statement: For a localizer W, every categorically contractible category is W-aspherical.
repair: Under L1 and L2, a contraction is a finite zigzag of natural transformations joining id_A to a constant functor; interval invariance makes the contraction a weak equivalence.
notes: Footnote 4; this is categorical contractibility, unlike the stronger weak-contractibility assumption in L3 bis.

statement: Every categorical homotopy equivalence belongs to W.
repair: With L1 and L2, natural transformations preserve W-membership; homotopy-inverse composites lie in W, so L1(c) puts both functors in W. In particular both members of an adjunction lie in W, using its unit and counit.
notes: Footnote 4; expanded in recovered commentary p1–p2. No Quillen model structure is required.

statement: Naturally homotopic functors F,G:A→B have the same image as arrows QF=QG in Hot_W=Cat[W⁻¹].
repair: For a natural transformation H:A×[1]→B, both endpoint inclusions become the inverse of the projection A×[1]→A under L2; hence QF=QG. Extend along a zigzag of natural transformations.
notes: Footnote 4; equality is in the ordinary localization of Cat, not a claim that F and G are equal before localization. Commentary p1–p2.

statement: Hot_W is the ordinary localization Cat[W⁻¹], with canonical localization functor Q:Cat→Hot_W.
notes: Footnote 4 and displayed functor before Lb; universe conventions are required if size matters.

statement: L1, L2 bis and original L5 imply L1, L2, L3, original L4 and original L5.
gap_or_error: The source states the implication without the intermediate constructions.
repair: Recovered commentary p2 supplies a proof: apply original L5 to [1]×A→A to obtain L2; use units and counits for adjunction invariance and L3; use the opposite twisted-arrow category to prove opposite invariance; apply original L5 to the opposite comma resolution to obtain even relative L4 bis.
notes: The expanded proof uses original L5, not the later fibre-detection axiom. This is a source-stated assertion with a completed proof in the commentary.

statement: Under L1, L3 and original absolute L4, the source claims f∈W if and only if fᵒᵖ∈W, and consequently derives dual L3′ and dual L4′.
gap_or_error: The proof is an appeal to the construction in Chapter I, ms72–75, which is outside this excerpt; the literal weakest package is not independently re-proved here.
repair: Recovered commentary p2 proves opposite invariance under L1, L2 bis and original L5 using two fibrations from the opposite twisted-arrow category with contractible fibres. Under modern relative axioms, use the corresponding standard localizer result. No logical-independence conclusion is asserted.
notes: “En appliquant la construction de I, p.72–75”.

statement: La: every f∈W induces a bijection π₀(f); equivalently W⊆W₀, where W₀ denotes functors inducing bijections on connected components.
notes: Listed as a complementary axiom on ms2 and invoked in the provisional connected-component reduction on ms23. It is not implied by W∞⊆W alone.

statement: Lb: Q:Cat→Hot_W preserves finite coproducts.
repair: Recovered commentary p3 proves Lb from L1, L2 and relative L4 bis: W is closed under indexed coproducts, so the coproduct/diagonal adjunction descends to the localization.
notes: Complementary axiom; Cisinski (2004), Proposition 1.1.5, supplies the relevant closure result under the modern hypotheses.

statement: Lc: Q:Cat→Hot_W preserves finite products.
repair: Recovered commentary p3 proves closure of W under product with a category by relative L4 bis, then descends the diagonal/product adjunction. The initial and terminal object adjunctions descend as well.
notes: Complementary axiom; preservation here concerns ordinary finite products, not an assertion about arbitrary homotopy limits.

statement: Which concrete conditions on W ensure preservation of finite coproducts and finite products by Cat→Hot_W?
repair: Answered sufficiently, without a minimality claim, in recovered commentary p3 under L1, L2 and relative L4 bis. Closure of weak equivalences and descent of the relevant adjunctions establish the universal properties after localization.
notes: “Il faudrait quand même dégager des conditions concrètes”; this paragraph precedes the ms3 marker, although it is on printed p3.

statement: The source proposes the sandwich W∞⊆W⊆W₀ as a reasonable combination of L3 quater and La.
notes: The lower inclusion is adopted explicitly at ms7. The upper inclusion is essential in the later characterization of W∞ and must not be silently dropped.

statement: For a base category S, Cat(S)=Fun(Sᵒᵖ,Cat) is the ordinary category of strict contravariant Cat-valued functors and strict natural transformations.
notes: Displayed definition of M(S).

statement: W_S in Fun(Sᵒᵖ,Cat) consists of natural transformations u with u_s∈W for every object s∈S.
notes: The initial pointwise weak-equivalence class.

statement: HOT_W(S)=Fun(Sᵒᵖ,Cat)[W_S⁻¹].
gap_or_error: This formula alone does not verify the derivator axioms, including derived Kan extensions; those are not proved in this passage.
repair: Regard this as the proposed diagram-localization construction. Further derivator claims require the corresponding existence and comparison results under their own hypotheses.
notes: “On doit poser”; distinguish HOT_W(S) from the single category Hot_W.

statement: A normalized splitting of a Grothendieck fibration X→S chooses Cartesian lifts, hence pullback functors u*:X_s→X_t for u:t→s, with id*=id and (vu)*=u*v* strictly. Fibsc(S) has such objects and functors preserving the chosen lifts strictly.
gap_or_error: The first printed direction X_t→X_s for u:t→s is reversed; the edition itself corrects it. Preservation of arbitrary Cartesian arrows is weaker than preservation of chosen lifts.
repair: Use u*:X_s→X_t and distinguish strict splitting-preserving maps from Cartesian functors. The latter distinction is necessary for the correction of the assertions on ms26.
notes: Editorial “[plutôt u*:X_s→X_t]”; recovered commentary p4; SGA 1, Exposé VI, §§8–9.

statement: The Grothendieck construction identifies strict diagrams Sᵒᵖ→Cat and their natural transformations with split fibrations over S and splitting-preserving functors.
repair: For F, objects are (s,x), and a map (s,x)→(t,y) is (u:s→t,a:x→F(u)y); composition is (v,b)(u,a)=(vu,F(u)(b)a). The chosen lift is (u,id). These formulas prove the assertion and identify fibrewise weak equivalences.
notes: Recovered commentary p4 expands the source’s identification; SGA 1, Exposé VI, §§8–9.

statement: On Fibsc(S), W_S is the class of splitting-preserving functors inducing W-equivalences on every strict fibre.
notes: Displayed definition following (*); “foncteurs strictement cartésiens”.

statement: The source calls HOT_W(S)→Fibsc(S)[W_S⁻¹] an isomorphism of categories, rather than merely an equivalence.
gap_or_error: Literal isomorphism depends on encoding split fibrations by their fibre families. With arbitrary underlying total-category object sets, reconstruction is canonically isomorphic over S and gives an equivalence of categories.
repair: Adopt the fibre-family coding for a literal isomorphism, or state the canonical equivalence under the usual unrestricted coding. Recovered commentary p4 makes this bookkeeping qualification explicit.
notes: “bel et bien un isomorphisme”; no homotopical theorem depends on the coding convention.

statement: The diagram categories and their fibred variants carry natural 2-categorical structures, whereas the displayed definition of HOT_W(S) uses their underlying ordinary categories.
notes: “seules les structures de 1-catégories sont utilisées”; the source defers the issue of variance in S.

statement: The initial comparison theorem asserts that all functors of the thirteen-category diagram induce equivalences after the localizations specified on ms7, identifying strict-fibrewise diagram theory with coarse Cat/S theory.
gap_or_error: The assertion is false; the source itself withdraws it in footnote 6. A total weak equivalence of split fibrations need not be fibrewise invertible, even after localization.
repair: For S=[1], the split-fibration map {0}→[1] is a total W∞-equivalence but its fibre at 1 is ∅→1. Evaluation at 1 descends to the fibrewise localization and detects noninvertibility. The same obstruction holds when W⊆W₀. The valid later theorems separate coarse comparisons, fine comparisons and the locally constant subcategory.
notes: The hope expressed on ms4 becomes the explicit theorem on ms8; “C’est totalement canulé” in footnote 6. Recovered commentary p8 supplies the counterexample and its dual.

statement: The higher coherence discarded by ordinary localization should be recovered in relative internal Hom objects interpreted as ∞-groupoid stacks over S.
gap_or_error: This is a programmatic assertion, with no construction of the internal Hom objects or proof that an isolated ordinary category HOT_W(S) recovers all higher data.
repair: For W∞ the modern coherent space-valued diagram theory supplies the appropriate higher interpretation. The Hopf and trivial circle bundles over S² have the same ordinary Hot-valued monodromy but different total H₁, so the ordinary local system alone does not recover the coherence. Recovered commentary p7; Hatcher (2002), Examples 4.45 and 4.51; Lurie (2009), Theorems 2.2.1.2 and 3.2.0.1.
notes: “Mais ce qui est perdu va se retrouver”; no present open-problem claim is intended.

statement: Fib(S) and Cofib(S) denote the categories of Grothendieck fibrations and opfibrations over S, with all functors over S as morphisms; Cofibsc(S) is the dual split version with splitting-preserving morphisms.
notes: The large diagram and its explanation; the use of all base-preserving morphisms in Fib and Cofib is clarified explicitly on ms26 and ms53.

statement: Liss(S) and Prop(S) denote the full subcategories of Cat/S on the functors smooth and proper, respectively, in the categorical homotopical sense used in the manuscript.
gap_or_error: These notions are recalled by name rather than redefined in this excerpt; smoothness is not smoothness of manifolds and properness is not a point-set compactness condition.
repair: Their relevant consequence is that X_s→s\X is a weak homotopy equivalence for smooth X→S, whereas X_s→X/s is one for proper X→S; the appropriate criterion is stable under base change. See Maltsiniotis (2005), Theorem 1.2 and its dual.
notes: Recovered commentary p15 and p20.

statement: Parf(S) is the full subcategory of Cat/S consisting of functors that are both smooth and proper; these are called perfect fibrations.
notes: “celles qui sont à la fois lisses et propres (fibrations parfaites)”.

statement: Fibhot(S) is the full subcategory of Cat/S on categorical homotopy fibrations. In the universal comma formulation recalled on ms43 for W-fibrations, specialized to W∞, after every base change T→S each strict fibre of X×_S T→T includes by weak homotopy equivalences into both corresponding over- and undercategories; these fibres consequently model the homotopy fibres.
gap_or_error: The initial passage recalls the category by name; the universal comma criterion makes precise which categorical homotopy-fibration notion is intended, rather than imposing only a single-base fibre comparison.
notes: “les catégories Hot-fibrées sur S” at ms5–6; universal definition recalled at ms43 with footnote 26 referring to Chapter I, Definition 3, ms117. Compare the fibre/comma comparisons on ms21–24.

statement: The diagram’s object inclusions include Fib(S)⊆Liss(S), Cofib(S)⊆Prop(S), and Parf(S)⊆Liss(S)∩Prop(S)∩Fibhot(S).
repair: These are geometric properties of fibrations, opfibrations and perfect functors; the later comparison must still distinguish the morphisms and the localizing classes.
notes: Object-containment assertions encoded by the large diagram.

statement: Fibsc₀(S), Fib₀(S), Cofibsc₀(S) and Cofib₀(S) are the full subcategories of their respective un-subscripted categories whose transition functors are ordinary weak homotopy equivalences (members of W∞).
notes: The source explicitly says “Hot-équivalences” before changing to the more general W in the following sentence. The distinction is retained.

statement: All solid inclusion functors of the large diagram are fully faithful except the four forgetful functors Fibsc→Fib, Fibsc₀→Fib₀ and their opfibred duals, which are faithful.
gap_or_error: Faithfulness does not imply fullness, and forgetting a splitting does not identify strict splitting-preserving functors with all Cartesian functors.
repair: The non-fullness persists even after restricting target morphisms to Cartesian functors: on [1]×BC₂ the functor twisting a chosen lift by the nonidentity element is Cartesian but not splitting-preserving. Recovered commentary p26; SGA 1 supplies the splitting formalism.
notes: “à l’exception des deux (plutôt quatre) flèches verticales supérieures”. The separate false fullness assertion occurs on ms26.

statement: Read literally for arbitrary W⊇W∞, the source identifies transitions being Hot-equivalences with transitions belonging to W (ms6), and identifies Hot_W-valued local coefficients exactly with the index-0 split categories defined by W∞-transitions (ms33).
gap_or_error: For W strictly larger than W∞, W-local constancy does not imply ordinary homotopy local constancy. Only the implication W∞-transitions⇒W-transitions is justified.
repair: Keep the subscript-0 definition in terms of W∞, and use the following W-valued factorization as a consequence. Alternatively introduce a separately named W-locally constant subcategory. For example, for W=W₀ the diagram Bℤ→1 is W-locally constant but its transition is not a weak homotopy equivalence. Recovered commentary p7 explicitly makes the distinction.
notes: “cela signifie que ce foncteur transforme … en éléments de W” (ms6, confirmed in physical PDF p7 / printed p5); “ce qui signifie exactement que ξ est dans Fibsc₀S…” (ms33). The ordinary and W-relative hypotheses are kept explicit across the consolidated repetitions.

statement: If a diagram F:Sᵒᵖ→Cat carries every arrow to W, its composite with Q factors through the groupoid completion Π(Sᵒᵖ)≅Π(S)ᵒᵖ, yielding a local system F̄ with values in Hot_W; the covariant statement is dual.
repair: This is the universal property of localization at every arrow of S. The resulting ordinary local system forgets higher coherent transport.
notes: Displayed factorization through Π(Sᵒᵖ); commentary p7 contrasts this with coherent local systems.

statement: A homotopy fibration over S, hence in particular a perfect functor over S, determines a local system on Π(S) with values in Hot, and therefore in Hot_W under W∞⊆W.
gap_or_error: No construction of the transport is re-proved here, and this ordinary local system is not a complete invariant of the fibration.
repair: Recovered commentary p7 gives the Hopf-versus-trivial-circle-bundle example: identical ordinary local systems over simply connected S², but H₁(S³;ℤ)=0 versus H₁(S²×S¹;ℤ)=ℤ. Higher coherent transport retains the distinction.
notes: “Je rappelle qu’on trouve également un tel système local”.

statement: A smooth object over S determines a contravariant functor Sᵒᵖ→Hot, whereas a proper object determines a covariant functor S→Hot; composing with Hot→Hot_W gives the corresponding W-valued diagrams.
notes: The variance is part of the statement; these need not be locally constant diagrams.

statement: In the initial thirteen-category comparison, W_S is strict-fibrewise W-equivalence on every category except Cat/S; on Cat/S it is total (coarse) W-equivalence of the underlying functor.
gap_or_error: The same notation hides two different classes; this is the source of the withdrawn comparison theorem.
repair: Use separate symbols W_S^fib and W_S^tot, and later distinguish the two comma-based fine classes. The diagram contains thirteen categories, not fourteen.
notes: “Dans chacune de ces 14 [13?] catégories”; corrected count is explicitly reflected in the recovered report.

statement: The solid functors in the large diagram preserve the initial indicated weak-equivalence classes, including fibrewise-to-total preservation for Liss(S)→Cat/S and Prop(S)→Cat/S.
gap_or_error: The two latter inclusions require a local-to-global theorem; the proof via comma categories uses relative L4 bis and its dual, not merely an unexplained invocation of absolute L4.
repair: For proper objects compare X_s→X/s, and for smooth objects compare X_s→s\X; apply two-out-of-three and relative descent. Recovered commentary p15.
notes: Last sentence of ms7 is expanded as numbered assertion (1) on ms15.

statement: Relative functors in opposite directions induce quasi-inverse equivalences after localization when their composites are linked to the identities by natural transformations whose components lie in the respective weak-equivalence classes.
gap_or_error: For the geometric comparison this criterion requires actual membership in the chosen class, not just total weak equivalence of the comparison maps.
repair: The formal statement is proved in the lemma on ms11–13; it does not salvage the ms8 theorem when its hypotheses fail.
notes: General strategy following the withdrawn theorem; consolidated with its explicit use on ms11.

statement: The comma replacement Φ sends Fib₀(S) to Fibsc₀(S), and Ψ sends Cofib₀(S) to Cofibsc₀(S). More generally the appropriate comma construction sends a homotopy fibration to a split locally constant (op)fibration.
repair: For Ψ the transition maps are X/s→X/t; for a homotopy fibration these are W∞-equivalences. The dual construction proves the Φ assertion. This verifies the target condition left for checking on ms9.
notes: The earlier claim is justified by the argument in footnote 13 on ms21 after correcting its target category.

statement: Conditional on the other comparison equivalences, proving the four inclusions α,β,α′,β′ are localized equivalences reduces, by composition and two-out-of-three for equivalences of categories, to Fibsc₀(S)→Fib(S) and Cofibsc₀(S)→Cofib(S).
gap_or_error: This is a conditional formal reduction within the failed initial programme, not a proof that the coarse and fibrewise theories coincide.
notes: Paragraph beginning “Mais si on a prouvé…”.

statement: With r:Parf(S)→Cat/S the inclusion, define Φ₀=ΦrC:Cat/S→Fibsc₀(S) and Ψ₀=ΨrC:Cat/S→Cofibsc₀(S).
gap_or_error: The displayed formula initially lands only in the un-subscripted split categories; the locally constant target condition requires C(X) to be a homotopy fibration and the preceding comma-transition assertion.
repair: Use perfectness of C(X), hence the homotopy-fibration property, and the corrected dual conclusions on ms21. The more substantial preservation of coarse W-equivalences as fibrewise W-equivalences needs new L5 for general W.
notes: Formula (**); repeated construction is developed on ms27 onward.

statement: The perfect replacement C:Cat/S→Parf(S) sends p:X→S to C(X)=X×_{S,σ}Ch∞(S), with structural map induced by the target endpoint β and natural unit j_X:x↦(x,the constant path at p(x)).
gap_or_error: The two-sided path category and its required endpoint properties are imported from outside this excerpt, not constructed here.
repair: Treat the path-category factorization as an explicit external input: j_X is a weak homotopy equivalence and C(X)→S is perfect. Subsequent coarse-preservation arguments are formal from these facts.
notes: Announced on ms9; section II on ms21–22. Recovered commentary p21 and p24.

statement: Let F be a full subcategory of Cat/S through which at least one of Fibsc₀(S)→Cat/S, Cofibsc₀(S)→Cat/S or Parf(S)→Cat/S factors. With the coarse W-class induced from Cat/S, the inclusion F→Cat/S is asserted to induce an equivalence of localizations.
gap_or_error: The source’s initial proof programme unnecessarily relies on unproved fibrewise comparison data. The full subcategory must carry the induced coarse class.
repair: Natural coarse-equivalence units for the replacement functors and the formal lemma suffice. For a full subcategory containing perfect objects, the C-replacement proof on ms24–25 works using W∞⊆W and two-out-of-three, independently of new L5. For the locally constant split images use the analogous coarse units after the later construction.
notes: Corollaire on ms10 and proof opening on ms11; commentary p12 and p24. Consolidate later repetitions only if the localizing class remains explicit.

statement: For each pair (p,Φ₀), (q,Ψ₀), (r,C), preservation of the localizing classes and natural weak-equivalence comparisons for pΦ₀,Φ₀p,qΨ₀,Ψ₀q,rC,Cr with the respective identities suffice to prove the corresponding localized equivalences.
gap_or_error: The reduction is sound; the geometric comparisons in the strict split categories are the hypotheses still to be verified, and some proposed comparisons later fail to preserve splittings.
notes: The six listed composites on ms11; this is a sufficient-condition statement, not an assertion that all six comparisons already exist.

statement: Formal localization lemma: if P:(C,W)→(D,V) and R:(D,V)→(C,W) are relative functors and natural transformations in either direction connect RP with id_C and PR with id_D, componentwise in W and V, then the induced localized functors are quasi-inverse equivalences.
repair: The images of the two transformations are natural isomorphisms. No calculus of fractions and no triangle identities for the original transformations are needed.
notes: Lemme on ms11–12; recovered commentary p12 expands the formal proof.

statement: In the preceding lemma, if P factors as C→D₀→D with D₀ a full subcategory and V₀=V∩Mor(D₀), then P₀ and R|D₀ induce quasi-inverse equivalences C[W⁻¹]≃D₀[V₀⁻¹], and D₀[V₀⁻¹]→D[V⁻¹] is an equivalence.
gap_or_error: The printed domain of the restricted functor is once given as D rather than D₀; the edition corrects it.
repair: Fullness lifts the restricted comparison from D to D₀, faithfulness verifies its naturality, and the induced-class condition keeps every component in V₀. Use domain D₀ for R|D₀.
notes: The explicit calculation through iF=(PR)i is supplied on ms12–13; commentary p12.

statement: For a fully faithful inclusion i:D₀→D, postcomposition Fun(D₀,D₀)→Fun(D₀,D) is fully faithful; therefore a natural transformation between functors landing in D₀ lifts uniquely through i.
notes: The mechanism used to construct v₀ in the formal lemma. The displayed connector on ms13 is a plain line because its direction is deliberately unspecified, not a missing arrowhead.

statement: Opposite-category duality reduces the five proposed comparison pairs involving Fibsc, Fibsc₀, Parf, Cofibsc₀ and Cofibsc to the three fibred/perfect cases.
gap_or_error: This organizational reduction does not repair failed relative-functor or unit hypotheses.
notes: “D’ailleurs par dualité…”. The separate question about further reducing the Fibsc₀ case is registered independently.

statement: The comma constructions Φ and Ψ do not in general send coarse W-equivalences in Cat/S to strict-fibrewise W-equivalences in the split fibred or opfibred categories.
repair: For S=[1], {0}→[1] is coarse but fails the undercomma/fibre test at 1, so Φ fails this preservation; dually {1}→[1] makes Ψ fail at 0. Recovered commentary p8 and p20 give the variance-sensitive counterexamples.
notes: “je dois rectifier le tir… ne sont pas compatibles avec les localiseurs”. The correct comma classes appear on ms20 and ms41 onward.

statement: Can the comparison involving Fibsc₀(S), with Φ₀ expressed in terms of Φ and C, be reduced to the neighboring comparisons involving Fibsc(S) and Parf(S)?
gap_or_error: The fact that Φ₀ is a composite does not itself supply splitting-preserving weak-equivalence units; the initial fibrewise-to-coarse comparison assertions are false.
repair: Keep the reduction conditional on preservation of the actual localizing classes and on valid comparison transformations. The source later discovers the unit obstruction on ms30–39 and obtains the correct fine comparisons by the free split and localized-naturality arguments on ms54–60. This is a provisional source question, not a claim of a current open problem.
notes: Parenthetical “Peut-être le cas Fibsc₀… se ramènera-t-il aux deux cas qui l’entourent…”; source question separated from the preceding duality remark.

statement: Replacing Φ and Ψ by Φ′=α′Φ₀ and Ψ′=β′Ψ₀ is proposed as a way to make the initial localized equivalence argument work.
gap_or_error: Even when Φ₀ and Ψ₀ preserve the relevant weak equivalences under new L5, the necessary comparison transformations in the strict splitting-preserving categories do not follow; the global initial comparison theorem is false.
repair: Grothendieck identifies the failure of the proposed unit to be Cartesian or splitting-preserving on ms30–39 and ms52–53. The valid fine-comparison proof uses the free split construction and localized naturality on ms54–60; the coarse theory gives a separate locally constant part.
notes: “qui sauf erreur doivent marcher”; retain the conjectural status of the source proposal, with its later failure recorded here.

statement: For an arbitrary W satisfying the initially stated localizer assumptions, the source identifies total and strict-fibrewise W-equivalence on Parf(S), Fibhot(S), Fib₀(S) and Cofib₀(S).
gap_or_error: The total-to-fibrewise direction is not valid for every such W. It is the additional fibre-detection principle later named L5, and fails for homological and finite-truncation localizers.
repair: Restrict the assertion to W satisfying new L5 (in particular W∞). For integral homology, the perfect map B(ℤ[1/2]⋊₂ℤ)→Bℤ is a total homology equivalence but its fibre Bℤ[1/2] is not homologically trivial; recovered commentary p43 gives the calculation. Later repetitions made under the explicitly assumed principle must be read conditionally.
notes: “Or ceci coïncide bien (via un théorème non trivial…)”; commentary p21–p24 and the report’s homological finding.

statement: On arbitrary fibrations, smooth objects, opfibrations or proper objects over S, total W-equivalence need not coincide with strict-fibrewise W-equivalence.
repair: Over [1], the inclusion {0}→[1] between split fibrations is a total W∞-equivalence but not a fibrewise one; its dual gives the opfibred example. This also covers the smooth/proper enlargements.
notes: “Par contre, ce n’est nullement le cas…”; recovered commentary p8.

statement: Could the fibrewise and coarse localizations of the non-locally-constant fibred/smooth or opfibred/proper categories nevertheless be equivalent despite their different weak-equivalence classes?
repair: The answer for the indicated comparison functors is negative: fibre evaluation detects {0}→[1] as noninvertible in fibrewise localization, whereas coarse localization inverts it. The argument works for W⊆W₀.
notes: “Cela semble difficile à croire”; recovered commentary p8 and source clarification beginning ms25.

statement: Numbered assertion (1): for f:X→Y over S, if both X and Y are smooth over S, or both are proper over S, and every f_s belongs to W, then f belongs to W.
gap_or_error: The source supplies no proof here and footnote 7 suppresses the relative descent hypothesis used by the comma-category proof.
repair: Assume W∞⊆W, two-out-of-three and relative L4 bis (with its dual for smoothness). Compare strict fibres with the appropriate comma categories and apply relative Theorem A. This also proves preservation after arbitrary base change. Recovered commentary p15; Maltsiniotis (2005), Theorem 1.2 and dual criterion.
notes: This proposition allows arbitrary S-functors; unlike original L5, no Cartesian condition is imposed on f.

statement: Footnote 7 asserts that L3 quater and original L4 suffice for numbered assertion (1).
gap_or_error: The displayed proof via a map X→Y over S requires relative L4 bis; absolute L4 directly handles the special case Y=S, not the general relative argument. A missing implication is not a proved independence result.
repair: Use relative L4 bis explicitly, as Grothendieck later distinguishes it on ms44, or invoke the stronger L1/L2 bis/original L5 package from commentary p2 that implies relative descent. The recovered commentary does not label the unresolved weakest-axiom implication a current open problem.
notes: Footnote “OK si on suppose L3 quater et L4”; recovered commentary p15.

statement: The smooth/proper fibrewise-to-total assertion is stronger in its formulation than original L5 because it drops Cartesianity of f and allows all smooth or proper objects, not just Grothendieck fibrations.
notes: “Cela renforce considérablement la condition L5”; this is a comparison of the formulations, not a logical-independence theorem.

statement: Which standard axioms on W imply each fibrewise and comparison property needed in the subsequent construction?
repair: The recovered commentary traces fibrewise-to-total descent to relative L4 bis and distinguishes it from the later total-to-fibrewise L5 and pullback L6. W∞ satisfies the intended ordinary homotopy assertions.
notes: Parenthetical “À dégager… à quelles propriétés standard…”; the task is to separate hypotheses, not to assert the weakest list has been characterized.

statement: The directed path category is Ar(A)=Fun([1],A), also denoted Ch₊(A)=Fl(A), with identity-arrow functor i_A:A→Ar(A) and endpoint projections σ_A,β_A:Ar(A)→A; their pair factors the diagonal A→A×A.
notes: Section I, definition of Φ and Ψ. The printed general factorization’s final target Y is corrected by the editors to X.

statement: The strict fibre of (σ_A,β_A):Ar(A)→A×A at (a,b) is the discrete category on Hom_A(a,b).
repair: A morphism in that strict fibre is a commutative square whose two endpoint arrows are identities, hence only the identity square on a fixed arrow survives.
notes: The first fibre calculation in section I; expanded in recovered commentary p17.

statement: In general the combined endpoint map Ar(A)→A×A is neither a homotopy fibration, nor smooth, nor proper.
repair: Take A=[1]. The fibre at (1,0) is empty and that at (0,0) is a point although the base is connected. At (1,0), both relevant comma categories are nonempty (indeed points), so neither fibre-to-comma criterion holds. Recovered commentary p17.
notes: “n’a rien d’une Hot-fibration… ni propre ni lisse”.

statement: The endpoint fibres are σ_A⁻¹(a)≅a\A and β_A⁻¹(a)≅A/a.
notes: First assertion of the lemma; the identity object is initial in a\A and terminal in A/a.

statement: The source projection σ_A:Ar(A)→A is a split Grothendieck fibration with contractible fibres, and the target projection β_A is a split opfibration with contractible fibres.
repair: Precomposition gives the canonical Cartesian lifts for σ_A; postcomposition gives the canonical cocartesian lifts for β_A. Their explicit fibres have initial or terminal identity objects.
notes: Lemma on ms17; “scindée” is implicit in the canonical endpoint construction and explicit for its base-change version on ms18. SGA 1, Exposé VI, §11(a).

statement: Both endpoint maps σ_A and β_A are ordinary weak homotopy equivalences, hence belong to W under W∞⊆W; they are in fact categorical homotopy equivalences.
repair: The adjunctions β_A⊣i_A⊣σ_A give σ_A i_A=β_A i_A=id_A and natural transformations i_Aσ_A⇒id and id⇒i_Aβ_A. This proves the stronger statement under L1 and L2.
notes: Lemma and footnote 8; recovered commentary p17 supplies the explicit adjunctions.

statement: Corollary 1: i_A:A→Ar(A), a↦id_a, is a weak homotopy equivalence.
notes: Source proof: σ_A i_A=id_A and σ_A is a weak homotopy equivalence; apply two-out-of-three.

statement: For f:X′→X, let X̄′=X′×_{X,σ_X}Ar(X). Its objects are (x′,u:f(x′)→x); define π_f(x′,u)=x′, f̄(x′,u)=x and i_f(x′)=(x′,id_{f(x′)}), so f=f̄ i_f.
notes: Displayed Cartesian square and object formulas on ms17; the general construction specializes to Ψ over S.

statement: For this directed factorization, π_f i_f=id_{X′} and a natural transformation i_fπ_f⇒id_{X̄′} make i_f and π_f inverse categorical homotopy equivalences.
repair: The component at (x′,u) is the arrow (id_{x′},u); equivalently i_f⊣π_f with identity unit. The homotopy is in Cat, not generally over X.
notes: Footnote 9; recovered commentary p19 writes the adjunction explicitly.

statement: Corollary 2: f̄:X̄′→X is canonically a split opfibration with fibre X′/x at x, and transition along x→y given by postcomposition X′/x→X′/y.
notes: “non seulement cofibrée, mais canoniquement scindée”; its chosen cocartesian lifts are (id_{x′},v).

statement: Corollary 3: i_f:X′→X̄′ is a morphism over X and a weak homotopy equivalence.
notes: Footnote 10. The source gives f̄i_f=f and proves weak equivalence via π_f, whose fibres are contractible; footnote 9 gives the stronger homotopy-inverse proof.

statement: For p:X→S, Ψ(X) is the split opfibration with objects (x,u:p(x)→s), morphisms (a:x→y,v:s→t) satisfying vu=u′p(a), and projection (x,u)↦s. Its fibre over s is X/s.
repair: The chosen cocartesian arrow over v is (id_x,v):(x,u)→(x,vu); these choices compose strictly.
notes: The general factorization specialized to p:X→S; recovered commentary p19 records the full arrow formula.

statement: For f:X→Y over S, Ψ(f)(x,u)=(f(x),u) and Ψ(f)(a,v)=(f(a),v) define a strictly splitting-preserving functor Ψ(X)→Ψ(Y), strictly functorial in f.
notes: The commuting square of the maps f/s with postcomposition transitions proves the required strict compatibility on ms19.

statement: The maps i_X:X→Ψ(X), x↦(x,id_{p(x)}), form a natural transformation over S and are weak homotopy equivalences, hence W-equivalences.
repair: There is also a forgetful π_X:Ψ(X)→X with π_Xi_X=id_X and i_X⊣π_X. Thus the printed description of i_X as a morphism in Cat/X is valid when Ψ(X) is given projection π_X; it is not a transcription error.
notes: Recovered commentary p19 and the corrections ledger’s resolved doubt. Although i_X is over S, π_X generally is not: pπ_X(x,u)=p(x), while the structural projection is s.

statement: The strict fibre map of i_X at s is the canonical inclusion X_s→X/s, taking x to (x,id_s).
notes: Last displayed map of ms19; this inclusion need not be a weak equivalence for arbitrary X→S.

statement: Corollary 1: Ψ preserves coarse W-equivalences; in fact f∈W if and only if the total functor Ψ(f)∈W.
repair: The naturality square Ψ(f)i_X=i_Yf and i_X,i_Y∈W give both directions by two-out-of-three.
notes: The source states preservation; reflection is the same argument made explicit in recovered commentary p19.

statement: A map f:X→Y over S is W-equivalent locally over S when f/s:X/s→Y/s belongs to W for every s∈S; this is the class later called left-fine W-equivalence.
notes: “dans W localement au dessus de S”; this is distinct from the strict-fibrewise test for general objects.

statement: Ψ(f) is a strict-fibrewise W-equivalence exactly when all maps f/s:X/s→Y/s belong to W.
notes: This is immediate from the explicit fibres Ψ(X)_s=X/s. Total W-equivalence alone does not imply the condition.

statement: For f:X→S, the local-over-S condition is precisely W-asphericity of f: each X/s is W-aspherical under L3.
notes: The target comma category S/s has a terminal object; “Si Y=S… beaucoup plus fort que p∈W”.

statement: For the localizers of interest, being locally a W-equivalence over S is strictly stronger than being a total W-equivalence; therefore Ψ alone does not establish the initially claimed fibrewise-to-coarse comparison equivalence.
repair: The dual interval example {1}→[1] is a total weak equivalence but fails the overcomma test at 0. The valid comparison equips Cat/S with the left-fine class, rather than replacing it by the coarse class.
notes: Source explicitly warns against concluding Ψ(f)∈W_S from f∈W; recovered commentary p20.

statement: Corollary 2: if X,Y are proper over S, or both are homotopy fibrations over S, then Ψ(f) is a fibrewise W-equivalence if and only if f is a strict-fibrewise W-equivalence.
repair: For each s, the commutative square with vertical comparisons X_s→X/s and Y_s→Y/s has vertical arrows in W∞⊆W; two-out-of-three identifies f_s∈W with f/s∈W. The additional conclusion f∈W uses relative descent as in ms15.
notes: The source supplies the square and proof; footnote 12 refers back to assertion (1), and hence to its hypothesis qualification.

statement: The dual comma construction Φ(X) is the split fibration over S whose fibre at s is s\X, with transitions given by precomposition; it is obtained by exchanging the endpoint roles in the construction of Ψ.
notes: “Le foncteur Φ se définit de façon duale”; variance is contravariant, unlike Ψ.

statement: Footnote 13 literally states that if X is a homotopy fibration over S then Ψ(X) belongs to Fibsc₀(S).
gap_or_error: The target category is a variance slip: Ψ produces an opfibration, not in general a fibration.
repair: Replace the target by Cofibsc₀(S). The fibrewise transports X/s→X/t are W∞-equivalences, proving the corrected assertion. Dually Φ(X) belongs to Fibsc₀(S). Recovered commentary p21.
notes: Confirmed in attached PDF, physical p15 / printed p13. The source’s proof verifies the corrected target; the literal printed statement remains false.

statement: For a homotopy fibration X→S, all comma transition functors X/s→X/t induced by arrows s→t are weak homotopy equivalences.
repair: This is the local-constancy condition behind the homotopy-fibre interpretation; compare Quillen’s Theorem B as restated by Cisinski (2004), Theorem 2.3.2.
notes: The actual mathematical argument of footnote 13, retained separately from its false target label; recovered commentary p21.

statement: The two-sided path construction supplies a natural factorization S→Ch∞(S)→S×S whose paired endpoint map is perfect, and consequently factors every p:X→S as X→C(X)→S with j_X∈W∞ and C(X)→S perfect.
gap_or_error: These are results from the earlier path construction; they are invoked, rather than proved, in the supplied pages.
repair: Retain the provenance and hypotheses of the external path construction. Perfectness is stable under the pullback/composition used here, and the unit’s weak homotopy equivalence is part of the input.
notes: “La situation est plus jolie, car p_S est déjà parfait”; recovered commentary p21 distinguishes imported geometry from formal consequences.

statement: The perfect replacement is functorial in maps over S and its units j_X form a natural transformation id_{Cat/S}⇒rC, where r is the inclusion Parf(S)→Cat/S.
notes: “Ici encore, la construction est fonctorielle”; the naturality square is displayed immediately afterwards.

statement: For every f:X→Y over S, f∈W if and only if the total functor C(f)∈W, assuming W∞⊆W and two-out-of-three.
notes: The source proves this from C(f)j_X=j_Yf and j_X,j_Y∈W. It establishes coarse preservation and reflection without new L5 or L6; recovered commentary p21 and p24.

statement: For W=W∞ and a map between homotopy fibrations over the same base, total weak homotopy equivalence is equivalent to strict-fibrewise weak homotopy equivalence.
gap_or_error: The source appeals to the known ordinary homotopy-fibration theorem rather than proving it here.
repair: Use invariance of homotopy fibres under a weak equivalence of total spaces over a fixed base for the total-to-fibrewise implication, and fibrewise descent for the converse.
notes: “dans le cas W=W∞ on sait…”; this does not extend automatically to an arbitrary larger W.

statement: Desired numbered assertion (2): for f:X→Y over S with X,Y perfect, or merely homotopy fibrations, total f∈W should imply f_s∈W for every s.
gap_or_error: This is a desired property, not a consequence of the preceding coarse-preservation square; it fails for general localizers, including homological and finite-truncation equivalences.
repair: Grothendieck isolates this as the additional axiom L5 on ms43. It holds for W∞; the integral-homology counterexample and truncation counterexamples are detailed in the recovered commentary p43–p45. Perfect base-change stability L6 is a sufficient additional hypothesis by the conditional proof on ms23–24.
notes: “il reste à s’assurer d’une réciproque”; the register preserves the conjectural source status, recording later failures in repair.

statement: Componentwise lemma, assumed for the attempted reduction: f:X→Y lies in W iff π₀(f) is bijective and each induced component map f_i:X_i→Y_i lies in W.
gap_or_error: La alone gives only the bijection condition; the full componentwise criterion is expressly admitted here and discussed again as L7 on ms44.
repair: Under the modern relative localizer hypotheses, the relevant coproduct stability and relative descent establish componentwise arguments; for this fibre-detection proof the entire lemma is unnecessary, as footnote 14 observes.
notes: “en admettant le Lemme”; do not count this as a proof supplied on ms23.

statement: Assuming La and the componentwise lemma, the fibre-detection problem can be reduced to a connected component of the base.
repair: The reduction is dispensable: fix the chosen s and take a perfect contractible replacement of {s}→S. It already lies over the relevant component and contains an object above s. Recovered commentary p23.
notes: Opening sentence and footnotes 14 (“ne sert à rien”) and 15; La is not needed in the corrected fibre-by-fibre argument.

statement: For a chosen s∈S there exists a perfect homotopy fibration r:S′→S with S′ weakly contractible and a distinguished object s′ over s; it suffices to work over the component containing s.
repair: Apply the perfect replacement C to the map {s}→S. The unit makes S′ weakly contractible, and its image supplies the chosen s′. No assumption that all of S is connected is needed.
notes: The existence assertion and footnote 15; recovered commentary p23. The later use of a globally surjective cover can be replaced by this pointwise construction.

statement: Additional hypothesis for the attempted proof: pulling back a W-equivalence along a perfect functor preserves W-equivalence; the source also considers the stronger variant allowing every homotopy fibration as the base-change map.
gap_or_error: This is a genuinely additional stability property, later called L6, not a formal property of a general localizer.
repair: Keep the argument conditional on this stability. For the fibre-detection implication, perfect contractible covers of individual base objects suffice.
notes: “Supposons qu’on sache…” on ms23 and the displayed pullback assertion on ms24; later axiom formulation is owned by ms43.

statement: The source conjectures on ms23 that perfect-base-change stability should hold for the finite homotopy-truncation localizers W_i, and on ms45 asks whether they satisfy new L5, L6 and L6 bis.
gap_or_error: The conjecture is false for finite truncation; later annotations withdraw the expectation.
repair: For nonzero A and finite n, a perfect replacement P→K(A,n+1) of the point has contractible total category and fibre of type K(A,n). The projection is a W_n-equivalence but its fibre is not, disproving new L5; pulling the projection back along itself disproves L6, and therefore also the stronger L6 bis. Grothendieck explicitly withdraws the expectation in footnote 32 on ms45; recovered commentary at ms43–45 expands the counterexample.
notes: “Ça doit être vrai pour les W_i” (ms23); “Il faudrait que je m’assure…” and footnote 32 “C’est faux” (ms45). Repeated expectation consolidated with both locations and the expanded later axiom list explicit; historical conjectured status is retained.

statement: Perfect-base-change stability of W-equivalences fails for k-homological equivalence, as already observed in Chapter I, ms87 onward.
gap_or_error: The earlier counterexample is cited but not reproduced in this passage.
repair: The recovered commentary’s finite action-groupoid covering, with the covering degree invertible in k, gives a total k-homology equivalence whose pullback along a contractible perfect cover exposes a nontrivial discrete fibre. The integral example uses B(ℤ[1/2]⋊₂ℤ)→Bℤ.
notes: “on a vu que c’était faux pour l’équivalence k-homologique”; no claim that the earlier package was independently re-audited.

statement: After pullback to a weakly contractible base S′, a homotopy fibration X′→S′ has each strict fibre X′_{s′}→X′ a weak homotopy equivalence; similarly for Y′.
repair: The strict fibre models the homotopy fibre, and {s′}→S′ is a weak homotopy equivalence. Stability of the homotopy-fibration property under base change supplies the needed hypothesis.
notes: The two vertical weak equivalences in the commutative square before the ms24 marker; recovered commentary p23.

statement: From a commutative square with vertical weak homotopy equivalences and lower horizontal map f′ merely in W, the source concludes that the upper fibre map f′_{s′} is also a weak homotopy equivalence.
gap_or_error: Two-out-of-three gives f′_{s′}∈W, not f′_{s′}∈W∞, unless f′ itself is known to lie in W∞. For a larger W this strengthening is false.
repair: Replace “Hot-equivalence” for the upper horizontal map by “W-equivalence”. This weaker conclusion is exactly what the conditional proof needs, and follows since the vertical maps lie in W∞⊆W. Recovered commentary p23–p24.
notes: “ce sont des Hot-équivalences, donc aussi X′_{s′}→Y′_{s′}”; confirmed in PDF physical p17 / printed p15. The subsequent correct W-conclusion does not validate the stronger intermediate assertion.

statement: Conditional fibre-detection theorem: assume W∞⊆W, two-out-of-three and stability of W under pullback along perfect functors. If X,Y are homotopy fibrations over S and f:X→Y belongs to W, then every f_s belongs to W.
gap_or_error: The source inserts an unjustified stronger Hot-equivalence conclusion in the intermediate square; the required weaker W-conclusion nevertheless follows directly. The printed connectedness/surjectivity reduction is avoidable.
repair: For each s use the perfect replacement of {s}→S, pull back f, and compare the fibre with the total category over the contractible new base. Three sides of the square lie in W, so the fourth does. This is precisely the later implication L6⇒new L5, with no use of La or the componentwise lemma. Recovered commentary p23–p24.
notes: The explicit square, ensuing W-conclusion and “qed” are on ms23–24; ms43 recalls the implication L6⇒new L5 as proved “à un ε près”, referring to the component lemma. The corrected pointwise proof needs no such lemma. The false stronger inference has its own separate record.

statement: The source says that the desired fibre-detection principle is needed to make C compatible with the chosen localizers.
gap_or_error: This necessity concerns the functor from coarse Cat/S to fibrewise-localized Parf(S), not coarse compatibility, already proved formally on ms22.
repair: State the target weak-equivalence class. Coarse preservation of C needs only naturality and j∈W∞⊆W; coarse-to-fibrewise preservation uses new L5 (or a sufficient hypothesis such as L6). Recovered commentary p24.
notes: “il nous faut absolument (2)”; the distinction is essential to the valid coarse comparison theorem on ms25.

statement: The perfect-replacement units define j:id_{Cat/S}⇒rC with every j_X∈W; restricting to perfect objects defines j′:id_{Parf(S)}⇒Cr, again componentwise in W.
notes: The two displayed natural transformations on ms24. They immediately prove the coarse comparison by the formal localization lemma, without a new fibre-detection axiom.

statement: For perfect X→S, the restricted unit j′_X:X→C(X) is a strict-fibrewise W-equivalence.
gap_or_error: The source invokes the unproved general inference from total W-equivalence between perfect objects to fibrewise W-equivalence. For this particular map a stronger fact already available suffices.
repair: j′_X is a W∞-equivalence, not merely a W-equivalence, and both source and target are homotopy fibrations. Ordinary homotopy-fibre invariance therefore makes its fibre maps W∞-equivalences, hence W-equivalences. This proves the assertion without assuming general new L5, while preserving the gap in the printed justification.
notes: Final sentence before the ms25 marker; recovered commentary p24. Do not extrapolate this special unit argument to an arbitrary total W-equivalence.

statement: Let C:Cat/S→Parf(S) be the natural perfect replacement with j_X:X→C(X) in W∞, and let r be inclusion. If W contains W∞ and has two-out-of-three, C and r induce mutually inverse equivalences between the localizations at underlying-total W-equivalences.
gap_or_error: The preceding argument also sought fibrewise compatibility of C; that stronger requirement is unnecessary for this coarse comparison.
repair: The recovered commentary at p24 separates the formal proof: C(f)j_X=j_Yf implies f∈W iff C(f)∈W, and the two restrictions of j become natural isomorphisms after coarse localization. No new-L5 or pullback axiom is needed.
notes: Source: “les foncteurs r et C induisent des équivalences quasi-inverses”; commentary p24. Ownership begins at the conclusion on p25; construction and conditional fibre argument occur on pp21–24.

statement: Assume W∞⊆W and two-out-of-three, and let C:Cat/S→Parf(S) be a natural perfect replacement with natural unit j_X:X→C(X) in W∞. If a full subcategory F⊆Cat/S contains every perfect object over S, inclusion induces F[W_tot^-1]≃(Cat/S)[W_tot^-1]. In particular this holds for Liss(S), Fibhot(S), and Prop(S) with their coarse classes.
repair: Factor C through F and apply the localization lemma of pp11–13 to the natural weak-equivalence units. The recovered p24 commentary proves this without fibre-detection hypotheses.
notes: Source: “pour toute sous-catégorie pleine F ... contenant Parf S”; commentary p24. The listed three applications are consolidated with the quantified theorem.

statement: To compare smooth, proper, fibred, or cofibred objects with the coarse localization of Cat/S, the relevant class is the class of underlying-total W-equivalences; the earlier claim that strict-fibre equivalences suffice on those entire categories is withdrawn.
repair: For W=W∞, the map {0}→[1] over [1] is a coarse equivalence between split fibrations but fails on the fibre over 1. The opposite example treats split opfibrations and proper objects.
notes: Source: “comme je l’avais annoncé à tort”; commentary p32. The earlier erroneous universal comparison is registered at its own source occurrence.

statement: For W=W∞, does localizing smooth or fibred objects over S at strict-fibre weak equivalences give a category different from (Cat/S)[W_tot^-1], and likewise for proper or cofibred objects?
repair: The recovered p32 commentary answers yes in general: over [1], {0}→[1] is inverted coarsely but not fibrewise, since evaluation at 1 sends it to ∅→*. Dualize for the proper/cofibred side.
notes: Source: “Il faudrait que je me convainque ... n’est pas une équivalence”. The question is historical and is not presently open.

statement: Assuming W∞⊆W, relative descent, and the provisional total-to-fibre principle later named the new L5, the coarse, strict-fibre, left-fine, and right-fine classes agree on Fibhot(S), Parf(S), Fib_0(S), Fibsc_0(S), Cofib_0(S), and Cofibsc_0(S).
gap_or_error: The equalities used on pp26 and 36 are conditional on the unproved fibre-detection principle of p22; they do not follow from the original L5 alone.
repair: Proposition 1 on pp41–43 proves fibrewise=left-fine=right-fine and implication to total; the new L5 supplies the reverse implication. The p47 summary explicitly restores “moyennant l’axiome L5”. Homological and finite-truncation localizers show why that hypothesis must stay explicit.
notes: Repeated internal-category equalities consolidated with all relevant locations and hypotheses. Commentary pp24,42,45,47. Does not certify an unconditional equality for arbitrary W.

statement: For constructing HOT_W(S) from a model for (Cat,W), split fibrations are localized at strict-fibre W-equivalences; split opfibrations use the covariant objectwise version.
gap_or_error: The phrase “principes généraux” invokes the construction of a derivator from a model; its existence is an input here, not proved for every arbitrary class W.
repair: In the ordinary weak-homotopy setting this is the homotopy category of coherent space-valued diagrams, contravariant for fibrations and covariant for opfibrations.
notes: Source: “suivant les principes généraux de construction d’un dérivateur”. The covariance correction is registered separately at p33.

statement: The forgetful functors Fibsc(S)→Fib(S) and Cofibsc(S)→Cofib(S), with strictly splitting-preserving source morphisms and arbitrary functors over S in the target, are faithful but in general not full.
repair: The recovered p26 commentary gives an explicit witness to nonfullness even after restricting to Cartesian target arrows: on [1]×BC2, fix both fibres and send (u,g) to (u,cg), where c≠1. This Cartesian functor does not preserve the chosen lift (u,1).
notes: Source: “fidèles, ne sont pas pleinement fidèles”; commentary p26. Separated from the false essential-surjectivity and full-faithfulness assertions in the same sentence.

statement: Every Grothendieck fibration over S is isomorphic over S to a split fibration, so Fibsc(S)→Fib(S) is essentially surjective as an ordinary functor; dually for opfibrations.
gap_or_error: Ordinary essential surjectivity asks for an isomorphism in Cat/S, whereas strictification supplies an equivalence of categories over S.
repair: Grothendieck, SGA 1, Exposé VI §9, supplies the group-extension obstruction. BC4→BC2 is a fibration, but a splitting would give a group section C2→C4, impossible because each lift of the nonidentity element has order 4. Replace “isomorphic” by “equivalent over S”, or pass to an appropriate homotopical/2-categorical comparison.
notes: Source: “quoique essentiellement surjectifs”; commentary p26. Verified against printed p16, physical PDF p18.

statement: Restricting Fib(S) to Cartesian functors makes Fibsc(S)→Fib(S) fully faithful and an equivalence of ordinary categories; the cocartesian dual assertion also holds.
gap_or_error: A Cartesian functor preserves chosen lifts only up to an invertible vertical comparison, not strictly. Restricting the target morphisms does not erase the splitting condition in the source.
repair: The recovered p26 commentary uses [1]×BC2→[1] and the twist (u,g)↦(u,cg): every cross arrow is Cartesian but the chosen lift is not preserved. Use pseudonatural/Cartesian morphisms on the split side, or the later localized free-split comparison, with object strictification interpreted up to equivalence over S.
notes: Source: “Ils le seraient ... si ... cartésiens”; commentary p26. The intended homotopical theorem is not refuted by this error.

statement: After restricting morphisms from arbitrary functors over S to coherent splitting-preserving ones and simultaneously restricting weak equivalences from coarse to fibrewise ones, the resulting localized categories might still be equivalent.
gap_or_error: This tentative expectation is false for the unrestricted split-fibration versus fibration comparison; it needs a local-constancy restriction. The source is still exploring the scope here.
repair: For unrestricted diagrams over [1], the walking-arrow counterexample {0}→[1] forbids the expected equivalence. Restrict to locally constant objects and retain the required coarse/fine identification hypothesis; that repaired strict comparison is proved later on pp55–60.
notes: Source: “Il semblerait donc ... catégories localisées équivalentes”; commentary pp26,32,40. The general unqualified expectation has already been withdrawn at p25.

statement: Define Φ_0=Φ∘r∘C:Cat/S→Fibsc_0(S) and Ψ_0=Ψ∘r∘C:Cat/S→Cofibsc_0(S), where C is perfect replacement, r forgets its perfectness, and Φ,Ψ are the two comma resolutions.
notes: Source subsection III and displayed formulas. The target restriction is justified by the following lemma; Φ has fibres s\X, Ψ has fibres X/s.

statement: If Y→S is a homotopy fibration, then Φ(Y) is a split fibration and Ψ(Y) a split opfibration whose transition functors are all weak homotopy equivalences, hence lie in W when W∞⊆W; thus they belong to Fibsc_0(S), Cofibsc_0(S).
repair: For Ψ the transition along s→t is Y/s→Y/t, a weak homotopy equivalence by the homotopy-fibration condition; the Φ assertion is dual. Perfect Y is a special case.
notes: Source “Lemme. Soit Y parfait ... ou seulement un Hot-fibré”; commentary p24 supplies the replacement context.

statement: The forgetful functors p:Fibsc_0(S)→Cat/S and q:Cofibsc_0(S)→Cat/S take fibrewise W-equivalences to coarse W-equivalences.
gap_or_error: This invokes the earlier fibre-to-total descent argument, rather than the new reverse implication L5.
repair: For split (op)fibrations use the original Cartesian fibre-to-total axiom, or relative comma descent with the appropriate smooth/proper fibre comparison.
notes: Source: “On sait déjà que p est compatible avec les localiseurs”; dual q stated in the same paragraph.

statement: Under the provisional total-to-fibre condition for homotopy fibrations, Φ_0 and Ψ_0 send coarse W-equivalences in Cat/S to fibrewise W-equivalences.
gap_or_error: The step “q ... W-équivalence, donc ... sur les fibres” uses the new L5 condition, not merely the original axioms.
repair: C(f) is a coarse W-equivalence formally. Its endpoints are perfect, so fibre detection applies; for Ψ use X_s→X/s and Y_s→Y/s, and for Φ use the undercategory comparisons. This proof is conditional on the displayed fibre-detection hypothesis.
notes: Source pp28 and corollary 2 pp20–21; commentary pp24,42,47. Does not assert compatibility with fine localizers for arbitrary W.

statement: The composite α_X=Φ(j_X)∘i_X:X→Φ(C(X)) defines a natural transformation α:id_(Cat/S)→pΦ_0.
notes: Source displayed α and triangle. Here i_X:X→Φ(X) is the comma unit and j_X:X→C(X) the perfect-replacement unit.

statement: Every component α_X is a coarse W-equivalence: i_X, j_X, and Φ(j_X) are underlying-total W-equivalences.
gap_or_error: The argument does not say Φ(j_X) is fibrewise a W-equivalence for arbitrary X.
repair: Use the natural weak-homotopy units and preservation of coarse W by Φ; compose the two maps. The source explicitly says “quoique non fibre par fibre”.
notes: Commentary pp24,30. This is not the one-sided-inverse/fullness error: that error occurs at p38, despite the recovered correction ledger’s p29 label.

statement: For X∈Fibsc_0(S), both Φ(X) and Φ(C(X)) belong to Fibsc_0(S), and Φ(j_X):Φ(X)→Φ(C(X)) preserves the canonical splitting.
repair: Apply the homotopy-fibration lemma pp27–28 to X and C(X); the functorial comma resolution gives a strict morphism of split diagrams.
notes: Source: “regardé cette fois comme flèche dans Fibsc_0 S”.

statement: Does the obvious comma unit i_X:X→Φ(X) give a Cartesian, hence admissible coherent, morphism when X is split and locally constant?
repair: The source immediately answers no in general. For X=S=[1] with identity projection, the image of the Cartesian base arrow has a noninvertible vertical comparison 1_0→u in 0\[1]. The recovered p30 commentary writes out the counterexample.

statement: The canonical unit i_X:X→Φ(X) need not be Cartesian: compatibility with transport supplies a natural comparison morphism which need not be invertible.
repair: Recovered commentary p30 supplies the explicit [1] example and compares the objects (u* y,1_s) and (y,u) of s\X. The later valid Cartesian comparison points from Φ(X) toward X.
notes: Source: “On voit tout de suite que non ... pas un isomorphisme”. The variance of its displayed illustration requires a separate correction.

statement: In the surrounding contravariant Φ construction, its transport square is the printed covariant square with fibres X/s and X/t and transport u_*:X_s→X_t.
gap_or_error: The square uses the fibres and variance of Ψ while the surrounding argument is about Φ, whose fibres are s\X and t\X.
