notes: Edition-level variance slip, verified at printed p19, physical PDF p21. A recovered ledger entry places a similarly described square at p51; the present square is actually pp30–31.

statement: When arbitrary functors over S are allowed, the same components define β:id_(Fib_0(S))→Φ_0p_0 with β_X=α_X, and each β_X is a coarse W-equivalence.
repair: Forget the strict splitting-preservation condition, so i_X and its composite are admitted. Naturality and coarse equivalence are those proved on p29.
notes: Source: “au mieux comme une flèche de Fib_0 S”; commentary p30. Φ_0 is here regarded as landing in Fib_0(S).

statement: If a full subcategory F⊆Cat/S contains Fib_0(S), or Parf(S), or Cofib_0(S), then inclusion induces an equivalence of its coarse W-localization with (Cat/S)[W_tot^-1].
gap_or_error: This theorem compares coarse localizations of full subcategories; it does not yet compare the strict morphism categories Fibsc(S) or Cofibsc(S) at fibrewise equivalences.
repair: Use ΦC or ΨC as replacement, with the natural coarse units α,β, and apply the pp11–13 localization lemma. Coarse preservation follows directly from these natural units without new L5.
notes: Source “Théorème-remballage”; commentary p30. The source says “équivalence sur les localiseurs”, understood as localized categories.

statement: The preceding full-subcategory argument does not establish the desired comparisons involving Fibsc(S), Cofibsc(S), Fibsc_0(S), and Cofibsc_0(S), because their morphisms must preserve chosen splittings.
repair: The free-split adjunction and localized-naturality argument on pp55–60 supply the missing comparison. Changing the morphism category is essential.
notes: Source: “échappent à nos arguments”; commentary pp26,30,40.

statement: For connected S, must every relative homotopy type ξ∈HOT_W(S) have fibres forming a local system in Hot_W, as the initial comparison would require?
repair: No. Over [1], the contravariant diagram ∅→* is a relative homotopy type whose transition is not invertible. Fibre evaluation shows it cannot be equivalent to a locally constant diagram. Contractibility of the base does not force arbitrary coherent diagrams to be locally constant.
notes: Source: “Il est totalement ouvert ... système local”; recovered commentary p32 resolves the question negatively for W∞.

statement: Every morphism in Hot_W is expected to be represented by a coherent arrow, that is, by an object of HOT_W([1]) under the underlying-arrow functor.
gap_or_error: This invokes the strongness/coherent-arrow realization property of the derivator arising from the stipulated model; it is not a theorem about an arbitrary prederivator.
repair: For derivators of model categories, Groth (2013), Definition 1.8, Lemma 1.9, and Proposition 1.30, supply strongness and the full, essentially surjective coherent-arrow realization. In the W∞ case use a model of spaces/Cat.
notes: Source: “toute flèche de Hot_W doit provenir d’un objet ... Δ¹”.

statement: The nine nonsplit categories of the p8 diagram, with coarse W-equivalences, should model the full subcategory of locally constant objects of HOT_W(S); passing from an arbitrary diagram to its total category and then C should give its locally constant replacement.
gap_or_error: This source conjecture still uses variable W and the provisional fibre-detection principle. For a general coarser W, identifying coarse total equivalences with fibrewise equivalences on local systems needs the new L5 hypothesis; the blanket extension without it fails.
repair: The chapter proves the comparison on pp55–60 and reflection on pp65–69 under the required hypotheses. For W∞, the modern realization is Ho(Fun(S^op,Spaces)) with locally constant part Ho(Spaces_/|NS|); take the homotopy category after the slice. Cisinski (2009), Proposition 3.10 and Theorem 3.13, establish the general derivator local-constancy inclusion and its two adjoints without identifying every coarse W-localization.
notes: Source: “doivent correspondre visiblement” p32 and C discussion pp34–35; commentary pp32,40,69.

statement: A split fibration over S determines a contravariant diagram S^op→Hot_W, whereas a split opfibration determines a covariant diagram S→Hot_W; there is no general canonical identification of these two fine diagram theories at the same base S.
repair: Apply the fibre functor and then localization. In the locally constant case every transport is invertible and the variance can be reversed through the groupoid completion; unrestricted diagrams retain noninvertible arrows.
notes: Source: “ce qui n’est pas pareil”; commentary pp32,50. Accidental equivalences for special S are not excluded.

statement: The category Cofibsc(S) is the outer opposite category (Fibsc(S^op))^op.
gap_or_error: Taking opposite total categories sends F:X→Y to F^op:X^op→Y^op and does not reverse the direction between objects of the category of fibrations.
repair: Delete the outer opposite: opposite total categories give Cofibsc(S)≃Fibsc(S^op), with the corresponding opposite fibre categories and their canonical splittings. The operation on functors is covariant.
notes: Source parenthesis “qui n’est autre que (Fibsc(S^o))^o”; commentary p50 and recovered report. Verified at printed p20, physical PDF p22.

statement: In the ordinary weak-homotopy setting W=W∞, a split (op)fibration is locally constant exactly when each transport becomes an isomorphism in Hot, equivalently when every transport is a weak homotopy equivalence; these are Fibsc_0(S), Cofibsc_0(S).
gap_or_error: For a larger W, W-local constancy is weaker than the ordinary homotopy constancy built into the subscript-0 categories. The literal general-W identification repeats the defect at p6 and is consolidated with that earlier false assertion.
notes: Source: “coefficients locaux ... signifie exactement”; commentary p7 distinguishes the two notions. This row records the valid W∞ case; the original broader assertion must retain its separate false-general-W verdict at pp6,33.

statement: The functors Fibsc_0(S)→Fib_0(S) and Cofibsc_0(S)→Cofib_0(S) should induce equivalences after localization, with quasi-inverses represented by Φ_0 and Ψ_0, under the standing fibre/coarse identification hypothesis on internal objects.
gap_or_error: The unit attempted on p30 is not a strict splitting-preserving morphism. A valid coherent comparison is still required at these source locations.
repair: Grothendieck constructs the free-split counit on pp55–60; the recovered pp56–59 commentary supplies the explicit adjunction and localized-naturality proof. Thus the source conjecture is resolved in the intended setting, not a current open question.
notes: Consolidates numbered conjecture 1 at pp33,35,37 and fn16. The replacement of Fib_0 by any full containing subcategory uses the separately proved coarse comparison.

statement: The inclusions Fibsc_0(S)→Fibsc(S) and Cofibsc_0(S)→Cofibsc(S), localized fibrewise, should be fully faithful, with essential images precisely the locally constant objects of the respective contravariant and covariant diagram homotopy categories.
gap_or_error: The source has not yet proved that localization creates no extra morphisms between locally constant objects. If W is larger than W∞, the index-0 definition and W-local constancy must first be distinguished; the intended identification is secure for W∞ or the later hypotheses forcing W=W∞.
repair: The chapter establishes the relevant reflection on pp65–69. Cisinski (2009), Proposition 3.10 and Theorem 3.13, later proves the full locally constant subderivator and both adjoints for general derivators. Identifying that category with the coarse Cat/S theory is an additional issue requiring the chapter’s stronger W hypotheses.
notes: Consolidates numbered conjecture 2 at pp35 and37 with pp33–34 formulation; commentary p40. The literal outer-opposite expression is audited separately.

statement: The fine covariant theory and its locally constant inclusion are to be written using (HOT_W(S^op))^op, as printed in the p33–34 discussion.
gap_or_error: The outer opposite incorrectly reverses morphisms between covariant diagrams.
repair: Use HOT_W(S^op), without the outer opposite. The commentary p50 explains that the central display on p50 already has this variance; the contradictory surrounding prose and editorial formula pp50–51 are separate later occurrences.
notes: Source last display context p33 and first retraction paragraph p34; commentary p50. Distinct from the preceding false claim about the unlocalized split categories.

statement: After identifying the coarse localization with local systems, forgetting the strict diagram structure should induce retractions from HOT_W(S) and HOT_W(S^op) onto their locally constant full subcategories.
gap_or_error: A retraction identity alone does not establish full faithfulness or an adjunction. The covariant target has been corrected by removing the outer opposite, whose literal error is separately registered.
repair: The reflection lemma pp65–69 gives a fully faithful right adjoint to the fine-to-coarse localization; this identifies the proposed retraction as the left adjoint reflector under the chapter’s hypotheses. Cisinski’s later theorem also supplies a distinct right adjoint to the local-constancy inclusion.
notes: Source circled 2 on p34; commentary pp40,64,67,69. Historical conjecture retains conjectured status.

statement: In the locally constant comparison problem, Fib_0(S) may be replaced by any full subcategory of Cat/S containing it, in particular Fib(S), if all those target categories carry the coarse W-class.
repair: Apply the theorem-remballage p31 to identify their coarse localizations. This replacement says nothing about changing the source’s fine localizer.
notes: Source parenthesis in circled 1 p35 and beginning of p36.

statement: The opfibration comparison is the dual of the fibration comparison under S↦S^op and X↦X^op, so it need not be proved independently.
repair: Dualize the total categories and the chosen splitting data; preserve the direction of functors between those categories. This is compatible with the corrected covariant theory HOT_W(S^op).
notes: Source: “tout ... revient ... pour X^o au lieu de X”.

statement: Let A=Fibsc(S), A_0=Fibsc_0(S), and B=Fib(S). Define i:A_0→A by inclusion, j:A→B by forgetting the splitting, k=ji, and ψ=Φ_0:B→A_0; localize A,A_0 fibrewise and B coarsely.
gap_or_error: Compatibility of ψ with these classes requires the provisional fibre-detection hypothesis; it is recorded separately at p28.
notes: Source p36 commutative triangle and p37 localization. The temporary notation HOT_W^?(S) denotes A_0’s localization; HOT_W^lc(S) here denotes B’s coarse localization pending comparison.

statement: Before localization, i:Fibsc_0(S)→Fibsc(S) is fully faithful, while j and k are faithful.
gap_or_error: Faithfulness or fullness before localization does not automatically survive localization.
notes: Source “i ... (strictement) pleinement fidèle, j (donc aussi k) fidèle”; the localized full-faithfulness problem is kept as its own conjecture.

statement: With the stated choices of weak equivalences and the provisional fibre-detection assumption, all four functors i,j,k,ψ preserve weak equivalences and induce the displayed triangle and section on localized categories.
repair: i preserves objectwise equivalences; j,k send those to total equivalences by fibre-to-total descent; ψ compatibility is the conditional p28 argument.
notes: Source “Tous les quatre foncteurs ... compatibles”. The proof combines earlier results rather than establishing new L5 here.

statement: The localized functors satisfy a natural isomorphism k̄ψ̄≅id on the coarse localization of Fib(S).
repair: Restrict the natural coarse weak equivalence α:id→pΦ_0 from p29 to fibred objects and localize.
notes: Source displayed one-sided inverse; commentary p38. It gives a retract, not by itself an equivalence.

statement: If functors k:A→B and ψ:B→A satisfy kψ≅id_B, then k is essentially surjective, ψ is faithful, and ψ is injective on isomorphism classes of objects.
repair: Apply k and conjugate by the natural isomorphism to recover any morphism or isomorphism in B. Every b is isomorphic to k(ψb). The recovered p38 commentary spells out these valid consequences.
notes: Source valid parts of “donc ... essentiellement surjectif ... ψ ... fidèle”; separated from the false fullness inference.

statement: The equation kψ≅id_B implies that k is full on Hom_A(a,a′) for arbitrary objects a,a′ of A.
gap_or_error: A section controls Hom sets only between objects in the image of ψ; it does not identify arbitrary a with ψka.
repair: Recovered commentary p38: let A be a discrete category on two objects, B=*, and ψ select one object. Then kψ=id_B but Hom_A(a_0,a_1)=∅→{1} is not surjective. The valid statement is split surjectivity of Hom_A(ψb,ψb′)→Hom_B(b,b′), together with essential surjectivity of k and faithfulness of ψ. A later natural weak-equivalence zigzag id_A≃ψk supplies the missing equivalence.
notes: Source “induit des surjections sur les Hom(-,-)”; printed p22, physical PDF p24. Recovered corrections.csv labels this ms29, but source/commentary locate it at ms38.

statement: Under kψ≅id_B, failure of full faithfulness of ψ is equivalent to failure of faithfulness of k.
gap_or_error: The printed parenthetical “i.e.” is not warranted by a one-sided inverse: k can fail faithfulness away from the image of ψ while ψ remains fully faithful.
repair: Recovered commentary p38: take A=*⊔BM for a nontrivial monoid M, B=*, k the unique functor, and ψ the inclusion of the first summand. Then ψ is fully faithful but k is not faithful. A stronger equivalence k,ψ would imply both properties, but has not yet been proved.
notes: Source “ψ pas même pleinement fidèle, i.e. k pas même fidèle”; commentary p38. Distinct logical error from fullness of k.

statement: Define the alternative section ψ̄′=īψ̄ from the coarse localized theory to HOT_W(S); its composite with j̄ is naturally isomorphic to the identity.
repair: Since k=ji and k̄ψ̄≅id, j̄ψ̄′≅id follows formally.
notes: Source displayed ψ̄′=īψ̄=overline(iψ) and two-arrow diagram.

statement: Is the weaker comparison ψ̄′:HOT_W^lc(S)→HOT_W(S) fully faithful even if the intermediate localization of Fibsc_0(S) has not been identified?
repair: Yes in the intended W∞ theory and under the chapter’s eventual hypotheses: pp65–69 construct a fully faithful right adjoint to coarse localization. Cisinski (2009), Theorem 3.13, establishes the full local-constancy inclusion with both adjoints in the general derivator setting.
notes: Source numbered question 3; commentary pp38,40. A retract identity alone does not answer it.

statement: The essential image of ψ̄′ is expected to consist precisely of the locally constant objects of HOT_W(S).
gap_or_error: The source explicitly qualifies this identification with “sauf erreur” and asks that it be checked.
repair: Perfect replacement followed by the comma construction has weak-equivalence transports. Conversely, the later free-split comparison and reflection identify every locally constant object with such a replacement in the intended theory.
notes: Source parenthesis following question 3; commentary p40.

statement: To prove the local-constancy comparison it would suffice to construct a natural zigzag of weak equivalences, through splitting-preserving maps, from id_(Fibsc_0(S)) to ψk.
repair: Localization turns the zigzag into the missing natural isomorphism ψ̄k̄≅id. The later free-split counit supplies the comparison with the reverse direction; no claim of logical necessity of a strict zigzag is made.
notes: Source sought “W_S-homotopie” in the endofunctor category; commentary p38.

statement: On Fib_0(S), the simpler comma construction Φ already lands in Fibsc_0(S), so the extra perfect replacement C can be omitted when seeking the split locally constant comparison.
repair: Use the homotopy-fibration lemma pp27–28 and the coarse equivalence Fib_0(S)→Fib(S); this changes the representative without changing the localized comparison problem.
notes: Source “Φ(X) lui-même est déjà dans Fibsc_0 S”.

statement: For a split locally constant fibration X→S, does there exist, naturally in X, a zigzag of fibrewise W-equivalences through splitting-preserving Cartesian maps connecting X to Φ(X), whose fibres are s\X?
repair: Yes: the free split adjunction on pp55–56 constructs the Cartesian splitting-preserving retraction R_X:Φ(X)→X. Its components give the required fibrewise equivalence in the locally constant case. The recovered pp56–59 commentary verifies the adjunction and the localization naturality needed for arbitrary underlying maps.
notes: Source final question pp39–40 and “Je ne vois rien à l’horizon”; commentary p40. Historical difficulty, not a current open problem.

statement: A functor f:X→Y over S is a coarse W-equivalence if its underlying functor of total categories belongs to W.
notes: Source definition a); customary notation W_S or W_tot. Commentary p41. Later notation appears on p49.

statement: A functor f:X→Y over S is a strict-fibre W-equivalence if f_s:X_s→Y_s belongs to W for every object s of S.
notes: Source definition b); this is not a homotopy-fibre condition for arbitrary X→S. Commentary p41.

statement: A functor f:X→Y over S is local, or left-fine, if f/s:X/s→Y/s belongs to W for every object s of S, where X/s=(p_X↓s).
notes: Source c) p41; name “fine à gauche” p46. The comma convention uses arrows p_X(x)→s. Later notation W_S^g; commentary pp41,47.

statement: A functor f:X→Y over S is colocal, or right-fine, if s\f:s\X→s\Y belongs to W for every object s of S, where s\X=(s↓p_X).
notes: Source c′) p41; name “fine à droite” p46; condition restated p70. The comma convention uses arrows s→p_X(x). Later notation W_S^d; commentary pp41,47.

statement: A map over S is a universal W-equivalence if every pullback along every functor T→S is a coarse W-equivalence.
notes: Source parenthetical definition in Proposition 1(2). This is stronger than an unqualified total-equivalence condition.

statement: For W=W∞, pulling a coarse W-equivalence over S back along a homotopy fibration T→S, in particular a perfect map, preserves coarse W-equivalence.
gap_or_error: Footnote 17 is not a theorem for every fundamental localizer W; its extension to general W is precisely L6 bis, with L6 for perfect base change.
repair: Weak homotopy equivalences are stable under homotopy pullback. The p43 covering counterexample refutes the unqualified homological extension. The p41 proposition explicitly adopts W∞ before looking for general hypotheses.
notes: Source fn17 and p44 axiom L6 bis; commentary p41. This conditional reading preserves the source’s stated W∞ setting rather than silently imposing it on general W.

statement: Strict-fibre W-equivalences are preserved by every change of base T→S.
repair: The recovered p41 commentary supplies the formal proof: the strict fibre of X×_S T at t is X_(image(t)), and the pulled-back fibre map is the original one.
notes: Source fn18; no smoothness, properness, or L5 is needed.

statement: Assuming relative axiom L4 bis, f is left-fine over S iff f is a coarse W-equivalence after every base change by a discrete fibration T→S (a categorical local isomorphism).
repair: Recovered commentary p41: for each t, (X×_S T)/t≅X/p(t) by unique lifting. Hence the comma condition survives pullback, and relative descent gives total W. Conversely, the representable discrete fibrations S/s→S recover f/s.
notes: Source definition c), “et le reste ... isomorphisme local”; commentary p41. The source’s terminology means discrete fibrations, not a Grothendieck topology.

statement: Assuming dual relative descent, f is right-fine over S iff f is a coarse W-equivalence after every base change by a discrete opfibration T→S (a categorical local co-isomorphism).
repair: Dualize the discrete-fibration argument: representable S-under categories s\S→S recover the undercategory tests, and unique cocartesian lifting identifies the pullback undercategories.
notes: Source c′), “co-isomorphisme local”; commentary p41.

statement: Left-fine W-equivalences should be preserved by smooth base change T→S, extending their stability under discrete-fibration base change.
repair: For the appropriate W-smooth/asphericity structure this is the smooth base-change theorem: local comma equivalences transport along smooth maps. Maltsiniotis (2005), Theorem 1.2 and Theorem 5.4, supplies the modern formulation and its precise hypotheses.
notes: Source fn19 “devrait être stable ... lisse”; keep conjectured as a manuscript status. Ordinary smoothness is appropriate when W∞⊆W and the fundamental-localizer hypotheses hold.

statement: Right-fine W-equivalences should be preserved by proper base change T→S.
repair: Dualize the smooth base-change result for the corresponding W-proper/asphericity structure. Maltsiniotis (2005), Theorem 1.2 and its dual explanation, gives the precise modern statement.
notes: Source fn20 “devrait être stable ... propre”; commentary pp41–42.

statement: For a fundamental localizer satisfying relative comma descent L4 bis and its dual, every left-fine or right-fine W-equivalence over S is a coarse W-equivalence.
gap_or_error: The first proof identification with the old absolute L4 is corrected by fn25 and p44. The valid statement uses L4 bis, not the mere substitution of names.
repair: Apply L4 bis to f:X→Y over S, and its opposite-category dual for the right-fine case. For W∞ this is the relative form of Quillen Theorem A. The separate false-inference row preserves the original mistake.
notes: Source Proposition 1(1), fn25 and p44; commentary p44. Modern reference: Cisinski (2004), Definition 1.1.3 and Remark 1.1.4.

statement: If X→S and Y→S are both W-smooth, both W-proper, or both W-homotopy fibrations, then a strict-fibre W-equivalence f:X→Y is a universal W-equivalence over S.
gap_or_error: The step from comma equivalence to total equivalence requires relative descent, and universal validity requires the stated regularity to survive base change.
repair: After any T→S, strict fibres still give W-equivalences. Smoothness compares them with undercategories, properness with overcategories, and homotopy fibrations with both; apply relative descent over T. This argument does not use the new L5 or L6.
notes: Source Proposition 1(2), fn21 and fn27; commentary p42. Ordinary smooth/proper/homotopy-fibred objects satisfy the W-relative conditions when W∞⊆W.

statement: For W=W∞, or for W satisfying the new L5, all four tests—total, strict-fibre, left-fine, and right-fine—are equivalent for maps between homotopy fibrations over a fixed base S.
gap_or_error: Only the total-to-fibre direction needs the new L5; fn22 explicitly inserts this hypothesis for general W.
repair: Both strict-to-comma comparisons are weak equivalences. They prove the three fine/fibre tests agree and imply universal total equivalence; invariance of homotopy fibres proves the reverse for W∞, or it is the additional axiom for general W.
notes: Source Proposition 1(2 fib), fn22 and p43. Commentary pp42–43. This is the general map statement underlying the six-category corollary.

statement: For maps between W-smooth objects over S, strict-fibre W-equivalence is equivalent to right-fine W-equivalence, and either implies left-fine and universal coarse W-equivalence.
repair: Use X_s→s\X and Y_s→s\Y in W and two-out-of-three in their natural square. Repeat after arbitrary base change and apply the dual relative descent condition.
notes: Source Proposition 1(2 lisse), fn23; commentary p42. Maltsiniotis (2005), Corollary 4.16 and Theorem 5.4, provide the modern smoothness framework.

statement: For maps between W-proper objects over S, strict-fibre W-equivalence is equivalent to left-fine W-equivalence, and either implies right-fine and universal coarse W-equivalence.
repair: Dualize the smooth argument using X_s→X/s and Y_s→Y/s, then apply relative descent after arbitrary base change.
notes: Source Proposition 1(2 prop), fn24 and “Le cas ... est dual”; commentary p42.

statement: Proposition 1(1), which compares X/s→Y/s over an independent base S, is simply the original absolute axiom L4.

repair: The source corrects this in fn25 and p44 by introducing L4 bis. Recovered commentary p44 explains the distinction; modern fundamental-localizer definitions use relative descent directly. The stronger early package involving original L5 can prove the needed implication, but the printed identification itself is false.
notes: Source “1) n’est autre que L4”, immediately annotated “Non, il y a confusion”; commentary pp2,44. No logical-independence theorem is inferred.

statement: For the subsequent comparison of weak equivalences, assume W∞⊆W (L3 quater), in addition to saturation and the relevant relative descent axioms.
notes: Source: “nous supposons ... L3 ... sous la forme ... L3 quater”. This is an explicit standing-hypothesis adoption, not a new version of L3 quater.

statement: For a homotopy fibration X→S, both canonical inclusions X_s→X/s and X_s→s\X are weak homotopy equivalences, and this property persists after every base change.
repair: This is the homotopy-fibration input from the earlier chapter; it identifies strict fibres with both comma fibres. With W∞⊆W the comparisons also lie in W.
notes: Source beginning of (2 fib) proof pp42–43; commentary p42.

statement: A W-fibration over S is a functor X→S for which X_s→X/s and X_s→s\X lie in W for all s, and the same two conditions hold after every base change T→S.
notes: Source explanatory definition in (2 fib), fn26 referring to Chapter I, p117. This is the relative W-homotopy-fibration condition used in fn27.

statement: For maps between W-fibrations, the strict-fibre, left-fine, and right-fine tests coincide and imply universal coarse W-equivalence, without assuming the new L5.

notes: Source (2 fib), fn27; commentary p42 and recovered report’s resolved doubt. The diagram’s one-headed arrow is not an error.

statement: For a nonzero coefficient ring k in which some integer n≥2 is invertible, a coarse k-homology equivalence between perfect objects need not be a fibrewise k-homology equivalence.
gap_or_error: The source gives the degree-n circle covering as a topological model but does not spell out its categorical strict fibres.
repair: Recovered commentary p43 realizes it as the translation action groupoid X=Z⋉(Z/n)→BZ. This is both a discrete fibration and opfibration; X≃B(nZ), and H_1 maps by multiplication by n, so totals are k-homology equivalent. The strict fibre map is Z/n→*, inducing k^n→k on H_0, not an isomorphism. Pullback along the contractible perfect cover E Z→BZ also gives a direct counterexample to L6.
notes: Source: degree-n covering and “quand 2 est inversible ... ∃n”; commentary p43 “circle covering”. Hatcher (2002), Example 2.48, supports the standard homological method, not a priority claim for this categorical application.

statement: The integral-homology localizer is suspected also to fail the total-to-fibre implication for maps between homotopy fibrations.
repair: The recovered development block p43 proves the suspicion: let A=Z[1/2], G=A⋊_2 Z, and p:BG→BZ. Surjectivity makes p both a fibration and opfibration, hence perfect; its strict fibre is BA. Filtered colimits of cyclic groups give H_1(BA;Z)=A and H_i=0 for i≥2. The mapping-torus sequence with 1−2=−1 invertible on A shows p is an integral homology isomorphism, but BA→* is not. The proof is supplied by the recovered commentary, using Hatcher (2002), Example 2.48; no exhaustive-priority claim is made.
notes: Source “sans doute pas ... Der(Z-Mod)”; recovered development p43, “An integral-coefficient version”. Historical conjecture is settled affirmatively. The flattened recovered block’s final “A=0” is read as A≠0, as its entire argument and report require.

statement: New L5: if X→S and Y→S are homotopy fibrations and f:X→Y over S belongs to W on total categories, then every strict-fibre map f_s:X_s→Y_s belongs to W.
gap_or_error: This replaces the original L5, whose direction was fibrewise-to-total for Cartesian maps of fibrations. The two conditions must not be identified.

statement: L1, L3 quater, relative L4 bis, and the new L5 alone force W=W∞, with no component-preservation hypothesis.

Recovered commentary p45 proves the corrected uniqueness statement by iterating loop fibres of a perfect replacement: every W-aspherical category and every iterated loop fibre is connected, so all homotopy groups vanish; applying this to fibres of a replaced W-map shows W⊆W∞. Cisinski (2004), Theorem 2.3.6, likewise includes a component condition.
notes: Source fn28 p43 and final “NB a)b)c)+L5” in fn30 p45. The annotation attributes the later proof to Chapter XII p12; that continuation is outside the present excerpt. Commentary p45.

statement: L6: if f:X→Y lies in W and q:Y′→Y is perfect (smooth and proper), then X×_Y Y′→Y′ lies in W.
repair: This is the perfect-base-change stability condition needed in the contractible-base fibre argument. The categorical circle-covering example over coefficients inverting n shows it is not automatic for homological W.
notes: Source bold L6; commentary pp24,43. A stronger variant L6 bis follows on p44.

statement: L6 bis: pullback of a W-equivalence along any homotopy fibration is again a W-equivalence.
gap_or_error: For general W this is stronger in form than L6, which quantifies only over perfect maps.

notes: Source bold L6 bis; commentary pp41,43,45.

L6 implies new L5 by pp23–24, so the same conclusion follows. Do not read this as an axiom-free equivalence for arbitrary W.

statement: L7(a): for every set-indexed family of functors f_i:X_i→Y_i, the coproduct functor ⨿_i f_i belongs to W iff every f_i belongs to W.
notes: Source L7(a), adopted into the revised fundamental-localizer package p45. Includes reflection as well as preservation of coproduct weak equivalences.

statement: L7(b): if f:X→Y belongs to W and Y is nonempty connected, then X is nonempty connected.
notes: Source L7(b), “0-connexe”; adopted p45. Together with L7(a), this gives preservation of the complete set of components.

statement: L7 is equivalent to the componentwise criterion: f:X→Y is in W iff π_0(f) is bijective and the induced map on each corresponding pair of connected components belongs to W.
gap_or_error: The manuscript states the lemma without writing out the component argument.
repair: Recovered commentary p44 supplies both directions. Decompose Y into components Y_j and X into their preimages X_j. L7(a) makes each X_j→Y_j a W-map; L7(b) makes X_j connected and nonempty. Conversely use the coproduct condition. To recover L7 from the criterion, inspect components of a coproduct and use the component bijection for connected targets. If Y is empty, X is necessarily empty.
notes: Source p44 Lemma and p45 condition d); earlier p23 admits this criterion. Commentary p44 includes the empty-category edge case.

statement: Does the original absolute asphericity axiom L4 entail the relative comma-descent condition over an independent base, under the weaker provisional axiom package?

Modern definitions adopt relative L4 bis directly. This audit neither asserts independence for every weaker package nor labels it an established current open problem.

statement: L4 bis: for any f:X→Y over S, if f/s:X/s→Y/s belongs to W for every s∈S, then f belongs to W.

statement: Assume the revised fundamental-localizer package L1, W∞⊆W, relative L4 bis, and L7. Then relative L4 bis is equivalent to its dual: if s\X→s\Y is in W for every s, then X→Y is in W.

notes: Source final paragraph p47; commentary p47. No assertion is assigned to p48, explicitly nonexistent/blank.

notes: Source three diagrams p52 and the lists of categories they cover; application of the full strength of the localization lemma, not only its essential-surjectivity part.

statement: Rename the earlier path-plus-comma replacements Φ′:=ΦrC and Ψ′:=ΨrC, where C:Cat/S→Parf(S) is path completion and r forgets perfectness.
notes: Source p52 renaming paragraph distinguishes these composites from Φ_0 and Ψ_0 on p51; the lower-case c in one printed composite is read as the same path functor C.

statement: For the composites Φ′ and Ψ′, natural coarse W-equivalences id→pΦ′ and id→qΨ′ exist on Cat/S; after forgetting split morphism restrictions, natural coarse W-equivalences id→Φ′p and id→Ψ′q also exist on Fib_0(S) and Cofib_0(S).
gap_or_error: The latter comparisons are functors in the full categories over S and do not automatically lie in the categories with splitting-preserving arrows.
repair: The natural path and comma units compose in Cat/S. Apply the localization lemma there; use the free split counit for the remaining split categories.
notes: Source pp52–53 and the displayed id→Φ′p,id→ψ′q; ψ′ is the typographic Ψ′ noted by the corrections ledger. Commentary p53.

statement: Can one find an appropriate natural comparison between Φ′p and id in Fibsc_0(S), and between Ψ′q and id in Cofibsc_0(S), using the initial path-plus-comma replacements?
gap_or_error: The source says that this route appears hopeless because its candidate unit does not preserve the required Cartesian/splitting structure; this is not a general nonexistence theorem for all replacements.
repair: Grothendieck changes the route in footnote36 and pp55–56. The recovered commentary p53–57 uses the free split adjunction, with its counit in the correct morphism category.
notes: Source “on n’arrive pas à trouver … la difficulté, par cette voie, paraît irrémédiable”; status is the formulation of a proof-search question, not a current open mathematical problem.

statement: The forgetful functor Fibsc_0(S)→Fibhot(S) and the restricted comma replacement Φ_0 induce inverse coarse localization equivalences, with natural W-comparisons id→π_0Φ_0 and Φ_0π_0→id; dually the same holds for Cofibsc_0(S).
gap_or_error: The source refers forward for the counit and suppresses the splitting-preserving verification.
repair: Use the free split counit of the recovered commentary p56. The unit and counit are total homotopy equivalences, so their restrictions are coarse W-equivalences; no new L5 is needed for this comparison.
notes: Source footnote36 p53 and the third diagram p57; Φ_0 is defined on all homotopy fibrations here.

statement: In the square with p:Fibsc(S)→Fib(S), p_0:Fibsc_0(S)→Fib_0(S), and the horizontal inclusions α′ and α, equivalence of the coarse localizations for p,p_0,α implies it for α′.
notes: Source footnote37; the square commutes and equivalences satisfy two-out-of-three. Footnote38 notes that the direct comparison from footnote36 makes this square unnecessary, not false.

statement: Restricting Φ:Cat/S→Fibsc(S) gives functors φ:Fib(S)→Fibsc(S) and φ_0:Fib_0(S)→Fibsc_0(S) in the reverse directions to the forgetful functors p and p_0.
notes: Source dotted arrows in the p53 square; these are functors on all S-functors between the indicated fibred objects, with Φ(f) preserving the canonical splitting.

statement: If X→S is a homotopy fibration, then for every u:s→t the comma transport t\X→s\X is a W_infinity-equivalence. Hence Φ(X) is a split locally constant fibration; in particular φ carries Fib_0(S) into Fibsc_0(S).
notes: Source p54 first paragraph; repeated use of the earlier homotopy-fibration/comma-fibre criterion. This is a condition on transition functors, not only on the homotopy type of the total category.

statement: For every X→S, the comma unit η_X:X→UΦ(X) is natural over S and a categorical homotopy equivalence of total categories, hence lies in W when W_infinity⊆W; restriction gives id→pφ and id→p_0φ_0.
repair: The ordinary projection UΦ(X)→X is a total-category homotopy inverse, although it is generally not a functor over S. The unit itself is over S, which is all the coarse comparison requires.
notes: Source p54 second paragraph; commentary p53. The assertion repeats the earlier comma-unit construction with its role in this comparison explicit.

statement: For a fibration X→S with chosen normalized cleavage, define γ_X:Φ(X)→X on a comma object (s,x,u:s→p(x)) by γ_X(s,x,u)=u_X^*x; on morphisms use the unique factorization through the chosen terminal Cartesian lift.
gap_or_error: The source gives the object formula and leaves the morphism and coherence checks to the reader.
repair: The recovered commentary p56 specifies the morphism by the equation c_v γ(a,f)=f c_u. Cartesian uniqueness proves functoriality. For a split target, the strict splitting laws show that γ preserves selected lifts.
notes: Source boxed γ_X and fibrewise construction pp55–56; “fibrée scindée sur X” is the edition’s base-name slip for S.

statement: For a cloven fibration X→S, the pullback construction γ_X:Φ(X)→X is a Cartesian functor over S, and different choices of cleavage give canonically isomorphic such functors compatible with the chosen Cartesian comparison arrows.
gap_or_error: The source expressly omits the functoriality and coherence verifications. “Unique” is understood relative to compatibility with the Cartesian lift maps, not as absence of every possible automorphism.
repair: The recovered commentary p56 uses cleavage coherence and Cartesian uniqueness; no splitting on X is required merely for this Cartesian functor.
notes: Source p55 parenthesis and p56 “à isomorphisme unique près” and “Je me dispense de la vérification”; SGA1 ExposéVI §§8–9.

statement: A Cartesian functor between split fibrations is therefore compatible with their specified splittings.

repair: Require splitting-preserving morphisms in Fibsc(S). The recovered commentary p26 gives a Cartesian endofunctor of [1]×BC_2 that twists a chosen lift; p56 proves that the particular free-split counit does preserve the chosen splitting.
notes: Source p55 “une flèche cartésienne, donc (si on veut) compatible avec les scindages”; false inference kept distinct from the valid property of the specially constructed counit.

statement: The pullback retractions γ_X:Φ(X)→X form a strictly natural transformation on the full category Fib(S), allowing every functor over S and imposing no Cartesian condition on the morphisms.
gap_or_error: An arbitrary functor over S need not preserve Cartesian lifts; even a comparison by invertible natural transformations need not exist before localization.
repair: The recovered commentary p57 constructs a canonical possibly noninvertible θ_f:fγ_X⇒γ_YΦ(f) using Cartesian factorization. A natural transformation over S becomes equality after right-fine or coarse localization because A×[1]→A is fine. Thus the γ_X give the required localized natural isomorphism. Counterexample: S=[1], X=S, Y=S×[1], f(s)=(s,s); at (0,1,0→1), the two values are (0,0) and (0,1), which are not isomorphic.
notes: Source p55 “fonctorielle en X … sans se borner … cartésiens”, repeated p56 and used in the p57 summary. Commentary’s development label concerns this explicit localized repair, not a claim of priority.

statement: With a normalized cleavage, γ_Xη_X=id_X for the comma unit η_X:X→Φ(X).
gap_or_error: Without normalization the evident statement is a canonical isomorphism rather than a strict equation.
repair: Choose identity Cartesian lifts over identity base arrows. The object formula gives id^*x=x and Cartesian uniqueness gives the identity on arrows; the split adjunction has this normalization automatically.
notes: Source displayed equation p55; commentary p56 and p59. This is a statement about the comma resolution, not the later path unit.

statement: The retraction γ_X is a coarse W-equivalence because η_X is a coarse W-equivalence and γ_Xη_X=id_X.
notes: Source unnumbered footnote39 at the displayed retraction equation; two-out-of-three. The recovered corrections restore the displayed footnote number without changing the assertion.

statement: For every X→S and split fibration Y→S, restriction along η_X gives a bijection Hom_cart/S(ΦX,Y)≅Hom_S(X,UY), where the left-hand side includes all Cartesian functors.
gap_or_error: Cartesian functors may alter selected lifts, so restriction does not have the claimed uniqueness with this literal Hom_cart convention.
repair: Replace Hom_cart/S by Hom_split/S. The recovered commentary p56 proves the natural bijection: h extends uniquely by (s,x,u)↦u^*h(x), with arrow values forced by Cartesian factorization. This is the classical free split fibration adjunction, described by Gray and by Emmenegger et al., Theorem2.6; it is distinct from the splitting adjoints for an already fibred category in their Theorem5.4.
notes: Source boxed Homcart formula, proposed with “Peut-être est-il plus élégant”; the intended split-morphism adjunction is valid, but the literal assertion recorded here is false.

statement: For the intended free split adjunction Φ⊣U, the counit has type ΦU→id_Fibsc(S), and the unit has type id_Cat/S→UΦ.
gap_or_error: The source’s first unit display uses id_Fib(S), immediately corrected editorially to id_Cat/S; the proposed adjunction’s Hom-set also requires split morphisms.
repair: Use the repaired free split adjunction from the recovered commentary p56. Its unit is the comma inclusion and its counit is pullback along the chosen split lift.
notes: Source two adjunction arrows and editorial bracket p56; the repaired type is already supplied in the edition.

statement: The five coarse comparisons (Parf,Cat/S), (Fibsc,Cat/S), (Cofibsc,Cat/S), (Fibsc_0,Fibhot), and (Cofibsc_0,Fibhot) reduce by restriction and duality to checking the two pairs (r,C) and (U,Φ).
notes: Source three diagrams p57 and final “deux couples de foncteurs”; the two internal cases are restrictions and the opfibration cases follow by opposite-base duality.

statement: All functors in the five comparison pairs preserve coarse W-equivalences, and each of their ten unit/counit comparison transformations is componentwise a coarse W-equivalence.
gap_or_error: The source summarizes the result before fully checking the strict split counit; naturality for arbitrary unsplit morphisms must be localized rather than assumed.
repair: For r,C use the natural total homotopy-equivalence path unit and two-out-of-three. For U,Φ use the repaired strict free-split adjunction and γη=id; obtain the other pairs by restriction and duality.
notes: Source unnumbered footnote40 and the p57 diagrams. Commentary p53–57. The footnote count is ten comparison transformations, not ten categories.

statement: The four comparison transformations for Fibsc_0(S), Cofibsc_0(S), and Fibhot(S) are restrictions of those for Fibsc(S), Cofibsc(S), and Cat/S.
notes: Source “Les quatre derniers homomorphismes … sont simplement induits”; restriction is legitimate because comma resolutions of homotopy fibrations are locally constant and the unit/counit remain within the indicated subcategories.

statement: Assume L1, W_infinity⊆W, and relative L4 bis. If F is any full subcategory of Cat/S containing Fib(S), then F[(W_S^d|F)^{-1}]→(Cat/S)[(W_S^d)^{-1}] is an equivalence. Dually, if F contains Cofib(S), its left-fine localization is equivalent to that of Cat/S.
gap_or_error: The source derives this from the localization lemma and the fine comparison; the same omitted split-counit checks remain upstream.
repair: The functor UΦ lands in F and the right-fine unit restricts to F because it is full. The unit and the strict splitting-preserving counit supply inverse localized equivalences. Reverse comma directions for the dual case; no new L5 is needed.
notes: Source p58 first paragraph and p70 footnote45; commentary p59. Consolidated with all locations and the two different containment hypotheses explicit.

statement: For any f:X→Y over S, Φ(f)_s is literally s\f:s\X→s\Y; hence f∈W_S^d if and only if Φ(f) is fibrewise in W, equivalently right-fine in Fibsc(S).
notes: Source part(a) across pp58–59 and displayed biconditional; commentary p59. This gives both preservation and detection by the comma resolution.

statement: For every X→S, the comma unit η_X:X→UΦ(X) is right-fine: for every s, s\η_X:s\X→s\Φ(X) belongs to W.
repair: The source proves this using the local-coisomorphism base change s\S→S. The recovered commentary p59 gives an independent direct proof: compose the two base arrows to define R:s\ΦX→s\X; then RJ=id and id⇒JR, so the comma map is already a categorical homotopy equivalence.
notes: Source part(b), pp59–60; W_infinity⊆W suffices. This stronger fine unit must not be confused with the path-completion unit, which is only coarse in general.

statement: Does Φ commute with every proper base change p:S′→S, in the sense that its canonical comparison Φ_{S′}(p^*X)→p^*Φ_S(X) is an isomorphism?
gap_or_error: The source does not specify whether “commute” is meant strictly or homotopically, and says that the general proper case may ask too much.
repair: Only local coisomorphisms are needed and are proved on pp59–60. Strict categorical isomorphism for every proper p fails: take p:[1]→e and X=e; p is a fibration and opfibration, but Φ_[1]([1])=Arr([1]) has three objects whereas p^*Φ_e(e)=[1] has two. This does not refute compatibility after fine localization or every possible homotopical reading of the question.
notes: Source “commute à tout changement de base propre … C’est sans doute trop demander”; the elementary strict counterexample is supplied in this rebuilding and is compatible with the recovered p59 commentary, which bypasses the question.

statement: For a local coisomorphism p:S′→S, the canonical functor s′\S′→p(s′)\S is an isomorphism for every s′; consequently s′\(S′×_S X)≅p(s′)\X and Φ commutes with this base change.
notes: Source final paragraph p59 continued on p60; the proof identifies the actual comma fibres by pullback. Here local coisomorphism is the source’s unique-outgoing-lift condition, equivalently a discrete opfibration.

statement: For every object s of S, the projection s\S→S is a local coisomorphism, so it is among the base changes for which the preceding strict comma comparison applies.
repair: An arrow out of the target of s→t lifts uniquely by composition; hence the projection is a discrete opfibration.
notes: Source parenthesis “telles les s\S→S”; used in the proof of the right-fine unit.

statement: For a split fibration X→S, the counit γ_X:Φ(X)→X is fibrewise a W-equivalence and therefore right-fine.
repair: The source uses that X_s→s\X is a W-equivalence for smooth X and γ_s is its retraction. The recovered commentary p59 strengthens this: X_s→s\X is left adjoint to γ_s by Cartesian factorization, so both are categorical homotopy equivalences.
notes: Source part(c) p60; the assertion uses the correctly constructed counit, not the false arbitrary-functor naturality claim of pp55–56.

statement: After the coarse and both fine comparisons, the only previously announced comparison property still awaiting proof is full faithfulness of i and j.
repair: The remaining problem is resolved by the adjunction argument on pp65–69; no additional identification of coarse and fine equivalences on external border objects is asserted.
notes: Source final comparison summary p60; commentary p60 and p64.

statement: Under relative comma descent, W_S^d⊆W_S and W_S^g⊆W_S in Cat/S; restricting these inclusions gives fine-to-coarse localization functors along the fibration and opfibration borders.
notes: Source p61 displayed inclusions and V-shaped diagram; repeats p41–44 descent with the corrected relative L4 bis rather than the original absolute L4.

statement: For either chain Fibsc(S)→Fib(S)→Liss(S)→Cat/S or Cofibsc(S)→Cofib(S)→Prop(S)→Cat/S, the functors from fine to coarse localization are identified, up to the comparison equivalences, by the same identity-induced localization functor.
notes: Source p61 “essentiellement le même” and continuation p62; the commutative squares come from the same underlying inclusion and the relevant inclusions of weak-equivalence classes.

statement: Define ρ:(Cat/S)[(W_S^d)^{-1}]→(Cat/S)[W_S^{-1}] and σ:(Cat/S)[(W_S^g)^{-1}]→(Cat/S)[W_S^{-1}] by the identity functor and the inclusions W_S^d,W_S^g⊆W_S.
notes: Source p62 diagram; after comparison these are ρ:HOT_W(S)→HOT_W^lc(S) and σ:HOT_W(S^op)→HOT_W^lc(S), with corrected covariant variance.

statement: When the new L5 identifies coarse and fine equivalences on the internal categories, inclusions from any internal model into a compatible border model induce the canonical functors i or j; using Parf(S)→Cat/S realizes both at once.
notes: Source paragraph p62 continued p63 and display(*); the relevant right- or left-fine class is fixed by the selected border, and both choices are available in Cat/S. Commentary p64.

statement: Under L1, W_infinity⊆W, relative L4 bis, and the new L5, the composite Parf(S)[W_S^{-1}]→(Cat/S)[(W_S^d)^{-1}]→(Cat/S)[W_S^{-1}], and its left-fine analogue, is the canonical coarse comparison equivalence; new L5 makes the first arrow well-defined by identifying coarse and fine equivalences on perfect objects.
notes: Source display(**) and preceding paragraph p63; the equality is induced by composing the underlying inclusion with identity-induced localization.

statement: Under L1, W_infinity⊆W, relative L4 bis, and the new L5, the functors i and j are explicitly induced by path completion C:Cat/S→Parf(S), followed by inclusion into Cat/S and respectively right-fine or left-fine localization.
gap_or_error: For this reverse functor it is essential that C send coarse W-equivalences to fine ones; total equivalence of its unit alone does not suffice.
repair: The new L5 applies to maps between the perfect replacements, so C(W_S)⊆W_S^d∩W_S^g. The pure coarse comparison uses weaker assumptions, but this fine-valued construction uses the additional fibre-detection axiom.
notes: Source final paragraph and diagram p63; commentary p60 and p64.

statement: There are canonical isomorphisms ρi≅id_HOTlc and σj≅id_HOTlc; in the displayed Cat/S models, both composites are induced by C and may be identified as ρi=σj.
gap_or_error: These equations make i and j sections up to isomorphism; they alone do not imply full faithfulness.
repair: Invert the natural coarse unit X→C(X) to obtain the two isomorphisms. The later adjunction supplies the missing full-faithfulness argument; the recovered commentary p38 gives the discrete-two-object counterexample to inferring fullness from a one-sided inverse.
notes: Source first paragraph p64; commentary p64. This source passage states the valid retract conclusion, so it is not itself marked false.

statement: A functor F:C→C′ is a localization functor if, for Σ={f in Mor(C):F(f) is invertible}, the induced functor C[Σ^{-1}]→C′ is an equivalence.
notes: Source parenthetical definition p64; ordinary categorical localization, with existence understood.

statement: The fine-to-coarse functors ρ and σ are localization functors and are retractions, up to isomorphism, onto the common coarse category.
notes: Source p64 “des rétractions” and “foncteurs de localisation”; further localization of a category already localized at a smaller class yields localization at the larger class. Full faithfulness of their sections still requires the following adjunction.

statement: If a functor F has an adjoint G, on either side, then F is a localization functor if and only if its adjoint G is fully faithful.
repair: For the application use the reflective-localization criterion for ρ⊣i: the counit is invertible if and only if i is fully faithful. The needed adjunction and invertible counit are explicitly proved on pp67–69.
notes: Source “On sait d’ailleurs…” p65; the excerpt does not supply a separate proof of this general criterion. Lurie 2009 Proposition5.2.7.4 is the higher-categorical counterpart, not a source claim about the 1990 argument.

statement: Set A=Cat/S, Σ_0=W_S^d, Σ=W_S, and let C:A→A be path completion; thus Σ_0⊆Σ, and identity and C induce functors ρ:A[Σ_0^{-1}]→A[Σ^{-1}] and Cbar:A[Σ^{-1}]→A[Σ_0^{-1}].
notes: Source setup and diagram(*) p65; Cbar is distinguished from the underlying endofunctor C, as the editorial brackets require.

statement: Under L1, W_infinity⊆W, relative L4 bis, and the new L5, path completion satisfies C(Σ)⊆Σ_0 for Σ=W_S and Σ_0=W_S^d.
repair: C preserves total W-equivalences by its natural total-equivalence unit; its values are perfect homotopy fibrations, so new L5 converts their total equivalences to fibrewise and hence right-fine equivalences.
notes: Source displayed “vertu C(Σ)⊆Σ_0” p65, reused pp68–69; commentary p60 and p67. Do not infer this from the coarse comparison alone.

statement: To make Cbar a right adjoint to ρ, the required adjunction arrows should have the initially drawn directions id_coarse→ρCbar and Cbarρ→id_fine.
gap_or_error: These are the unit/counit directions for the opposite adjunction, while the construction only provides a generally noninvertible fine arrow id_fine→Cbarρ. The retained source diagram contains both directions after correction.
repair: Grothendieck corrects the orientation on p67 (and in footnote41): take unit id_fine→Cbarρ and counit ρCbar→id_coarse, with Cbar right adjoint. The inverse path unit exists in the coarse category, not in the fine category generally.
notes: Source p65 attempted arrows and footnote41, explicitly corrected on p67; commentary p64. The row records the rejected orientation, not a claim that a locally constant inclusion has no other adjoint.

statement: Let Σ_0⊆Σ be classes in A with localizations, C:A→A, and η:id_A→C natural. If C(Σ)⊆Σ_0, η_X∈Σ, and η_CX∈Σ_0 for every X, then P:A[Σ_0^{-1}]→A[Σ^{-1}] has fully faithful right adjoint R induced by C; the unit is η in the fine localization and the counit is its inverse in the coarse localization.
gap_or_error: No additional coherence hypothesis is missing. The source supplies the needed iterated-unit identity geometrically; the recovered commentary proves that it follows already from these formal hypotheses.
repair: The recovered commentary p67 sets T=RP, e:id→T, a=e_Tx and b=T(e_x). Naturality at e_x followed by T and cancellation of invertible b gives T(b)=T(a); naturality at a and b then gives a=b. Both triangle identities follow, and the invertible counit proves full faithfulness. The generally noninvertible e_x is never cancelled.
notes: The source proves the application through pp65–69; commentary p67 isolates its formal lemma and p69 gives the geometric proof. The full image consists exactly of objects whose fine unit is invertible. Compare Lurie 2009 Proposition5.2.7.4.

statement: The path unit η:id_A→C is natural over S and every η_X lies in the coarse class Σ=W_S.
notes: Source p66 first display and condition1; this repeats the established path-replacement property as an explicit formal hypothesis for the reflection argument.

statement: The ordinary projection π_X:C(X)=X×_S(Ch_infinity(S),source)→X generally fails to be over S, because C(X) is placed over the endpoint of the path, whereas X is placed over its start.
repair: Do not use this projection as a morphism in A=Cat/S. The counit needed later is the inverse of η_X only after coarse localization.
notes: Source p66 “ce n’est malheureusement pas un S-morphisme”; commentary p64 and p67.

statement: The path unit η_X:X→C(X) is not generally right-fine, even though it is always coarse; if it were fine for every X, every relative type would already be locally constant.
repair: The recovered commentary p70 gives the interval example: the contravariant diagram ∅→* reflects to *→*, with a unit that is a total equivalence but fails at the fibre over1. The reflector sends a general B→A to A→A; the separate right adjoint of the constant-diagram inclusion sends it to B.
notes: Source p66 and footnote42; commentary p70 computes the unit and explains why the adjunction orientation matters.

statement: If X is a homotopy fibration over S, in particular if X=C(Y), then the path unit η_X lies in Σ_0=W_S^d: this unit is already a W_infinity-equivalence between homotopy fibrations, hence is fibrewise and right-fine in W_infinity⊆W.
repair: For this particular path unit, W_infinity⊆W suffices, because its total equivalence is already in W_infinity and ordinary homotopy-fibre detection applies. New L5 for the larger class W is needed instead for the arbitrary-map assertion C(W_S)⊆W_S^d; the two uses must be distinguished.
notes: Source condition2 and preceding parenthesis p66; commentary p60 and p67.

statement: For the correct adjunction P⊣R, define the counit ε_X:PR(X)→X in A[Σ^{-1}] by ε_X=(η_X)^{-1}; the same η induces the unit id→RP in A[Σ_0^{-1}].
notes: Source p67 displayed p_X=i_X^{-1}; the inverse exists in the coarse localization because η_X∈Σ, and is not asserted to exist in the fine localization.

statement: To verify the proposed adjunction it suffices to check εP∘Pη=id_P and Rε∘ηR=id_R.
notes: Source two composite diagrams p67; ordinary adjunction triangle criterion. The source writes C for Cbar after explicitly declaring the abbreviation.

statement: For every X→S, the maps η_CX and C(η_X):C(X)→C²(X) become equal in (Cat/S)[(W_S^d)^{-1}].
repair: Grothendieck proves the statement by concatenation of finite paths and two-out-of-three on p69. The recovered commentary p67 gives a second, purely formal proof from naturality and invertibility of both iterated units. No outstanding coherence gap remains.
notes: Source boxed equality and named lemma p68, proof p69 across printed42–43; commentary p67 and p69. Equality is asserted after fine localization, not literally as unlocalized functors.

statement: In the path model, C(X) has objects (x,c:p(x)⇝t) and projects to t; C²(X) has objects (x,c:p(x)⇝t,c′:t⇝t′) and projects to t′.
notes: Source explicit object and projection formulas p68; morphisms are the compatible path diagrams from the previously supplied path-category construction.

notes: Source two diagrams p69; they insert the empty path at different positions, which explains why literal equality before localization is not claimed.

statement: Either Ch_infinity(S) or the finite-path category Ch(S) may be used for the path replacement, with the same resulting localized theory.

notes: Source p69 choice-of-path-theory paragraph; not promoted to a proof supplied on pp1–70.

statement: In the chosen finite-path model, paths admit concatenation and the empty paths are strict left and right units.

statement: Concatenation defines a functor μ_X:C²(X)→C(X) over S by μ_X(x,c,c′)=(x,c′∘c).
